Musicorum, le festival qui veut rendre le classique accessible à tous La pianiste Anna Shinyoung Lee, accompagnée par l’Ataneres Ensemble sous la direction de Yannick Van de Velde, lors de l’édition 2023 de Musicorum, le festival de musique classique gratuit au cœur de Bruxelles. - D.R. I l est 12 h 15, les portes de l’auditorium s’ouvrent tandis que Bruxelles poursuit son rythme habituel. Quelques employés de bureau, des touristes en shorts et des aficionados du classique prennent place dans les travées du grand auditorium des Musées royaux des Beaux-Arts. Pendant 45 minutes, le brouhaha de la ville laisse place aux sonorités d’un violon, d’un piano ou d’un quatuor à cordes, avant que chacun ne reprenne le cours de sa journée. A première vue, la recette paraît simple : des concerts gratuits, un format court et un lieu prestigieux. Pourtant, derrière cette apparente évidence se dessine une véritable réflexion sur les manières de faire vivre aujourd’hui la musique classique en dehors des grandes salles de concert et de leurs codes parfois intimidants pour le spectateur moins averti. Installé depuis plusieurs années, le festival Musicorum revendique une philosophie inchangée depuis sa création, il y a tout juste quarante ans : rendre la musique classique accessible au plus grand nombre sans négliger pour autant l’exigence et la rigueur artistique. Un concept né... à Stockholm L’histoire commence en 1982. Cette année-là, l’abbé Jacques Van Der Biest découvre à Stockholm un dispositif qui l’intrigue. Dans plusieurs églises de la capitale suédoise, des concerts sont proposés chaque midi aux travailleurs et aux visiteurs de passage. « En se promenant, il entendait de la musique qui sortait des églises. Il est allé demander ce que c’était et le prêtre local lui a expliqué qu’ils organisaient des concerts de midi pour les touristes et les gens qui travaillaient », raconte aujourd’hui Marjana Mandi, coordinatrice générale du festival. De retour à Bruxelles, alors curé de l’église des Minimes, dans le quartier des Marolles, Jacques Van Der Biest transpose, en 1986, le concept. Le succès est rapide. Quarante ans plus tard, Musicorum conserve ce même ADN, même si le festival a quitté les Marolles pour s’installer au cœur des Musées royaux des Beaux-Arts. Lorsque l’abbé transmet le projet à la nouvelle équipe, le mot d’ordre est simple. « Il nous a dit : “Il faut simplement être organisateur et garder le concept de base.” » Un principe auquel l’équipe actuelle est restée fidèle. Faire tomber les barrières du classique Si la gratuité apparaît comme le premier levier d’accessibilité, Marjana Mandi estime que le principal obstacle n’est pas uniquement financier. « Quand nous avons proposé des concerts à des enfants ou à des personnes issues de milieux défavorisés, certains nous répondaient : “La musique classique, ce n’est pas pour nous. C’est pour les gens qui ont les moyens.” » Cette réaction résume à elle seule l’un des défis auxquels reste confrontée la musique classique : moins une question de prix que de représentation sociale. Musicorum entend précisément déconstruire cette idée. L’entrée est libre, une participation volontaire est proposée dans un panier à la sortie, mais personne n’est tenu de contribuer. Plus encore, le festival investit un lieu patrimonial que beaucoup pourraient considérer comme intimidant pour mieux rappeler qu’il appartient à tous. « On leur dit que cet endroit est aussi pour eux, que cette musique n’est pas réservée aux musiciens ou à un certain milieu. C’est très important pour nous. » La musique classique n’est pas réservée aux musiciens ou à un certain milieu Marjana Mandi , Coordinatrice générale du festival Musicorum Cette volonté passe également par un travail de terrain avec des associations de quartier, des centres accueillant des publics fragilisés ou en situation de handicap, mais aussi avec des groupes d’enfants et leurs éducateurs. Pour Marjana Mandi, les effets sont parfois très concrets. Certains jeunes, après cette première découverte, choisissent ensuite de s’inscrire dans une académie de musique. « C’est un succès pour les enfants, pour les personnes en situation de handicap, pour des publics défavorisés... et surtout un succès de la gratuité. » Le format lui-même participe de cette ouverture. En limitant les concerts à 45 minutes, Musicorum épouse le rythme d’une ville où le temps constitue sans doute souvent le premier luxe. Loin des longues soirées de concert, ce rendez-vous quotidien s’insère dans une pause midi. Une temporalité qui attire autant les mélomanes fidèles que des visiteurs venus presque par hasard. « Le festival est ouvert aux familles, aux musiciens, aux mélomanes, à tout le monde », résume Marjana Mandi. Cette diversité est aussi le fruit d’un travail de programmation. Un comité artistique composé notamment des pianistes Jean-Claude Vanden Eynden, Eliane Reyes et Yannick Van De Velde sélectionne des œuvres adaptées à ce format condensé, sans sacrifier leur cohérence artistique. En creux, Musicorum esquisse ainsi une autre manière d’habiter la ville par la culture. Non plus comme un événement exceptionnel réservé à quelques initiés, mais comme un rendez-vous presque quotidien, intégré aux déplacements, aux visites et aux pratiques urbaines usuelles. Une approche qui, au-delà du renouvellement des publics, offre également une scène précieuse à une nouvelle génération d’interprètes, appelée à prendre le relais des grandes figures de la musique classique. Cette dimension constitue aujourd’hui l’autre pilier du festival. Le pari de la relève : un tremplin pour la jeune garde Au-delà de sa mission de démocratisation, Musicorum s’est imposé comme une vitrine essentielle pour les jeunes interprètes. Chaque été, le festival offre à de futurs grands noms l’occasion de partager l’affiche avec des artistes confirmés. « Le but premier, c’est de pouvoir, grâce au regard de notre comité artistique, repérer chez un jeune sa capacité future à se déployer », explique Marjana Mandi. « Nous avons accueilli ici des musiciens qui se sont ensuite retrouvés au Concours Breughel, comme Pierre Fontenelle. C’est évidemment un tremplin et cela leur offre une certaine visibilité. » Dans un milieu où les débuts de carrière dépendent souvent des concours internationaux, ces plateformes intermédiaires permettent aux jeunes talents de multiplier les expériences scéniques. A seulement 18 ans, la violoniste belge Alexandra Chepurenko en est pleinement consciente. Invitée cette année à se produire en récital, elle y voit une opportunité majeure : « C’est un festival qui grandit et devient de plus en plus connu. Beaucoup de solistes importants viennent y jouer. Je suis très honorée d’y participer et j’espère que cela va beaucoup m’aider dans ma carrière. » Je suis très honorée de participer au Musicorum et j’espère que cela va beaucoup m’aider dans ma carrière Alexandra Chepurenko , Violoniste belge de 18 ans A rebours de l’image solennelle du concert classique, le contexte particulier de Musicorum modifie profondément le rapport des interprètes à la scène. « Quand je joue à midi ou le matin, j’ai beaucoup moins de stress », confie la violoniste. « Je me sens beaucoup plus détendue. Le soir, je ressens toujours davantage de pression. » Le format condensé de 45 minutes impose néanmoins de vraies contraintes de programmation : « La plupart des œuvres du grand répertoire durent déjà quinze ou vingt minutes. Ce n’est pas facile de trouver des pièces qui dialoguent entre elles et forment un programme cohérent. Mais c’est un exercice très intéressant. » Pour Alexandra Chepurenko, cette proximité brise l’élitisme et favorise l’échange avec le public. « Ici, tout est beaucoup plus intime. Après le concert, je peux discuter avec les personnes présentes, leur demander ce qu’elles ont pensé de mon interprétation. Leurs retours peuvent aussi me faire évoluer. Quand je vais à un concert classique, je vois souvent un public plus âgé. Une « méduse tueuse » envahit une partie des côtes françaises Physalie. - Unsplash. L a méduse « tueuse », généralement présente en Méditerranée ou sur la façade sud Atlantique (notamment au Portugal), semblerait remonter vers les eaux françaises et plus précisément en Bretagne, rapporte la Dernière Heure . Même si l’on parle de méduse, il s’agit en fait de siphonophore (et plus précisément de physalie, un type de siphonophore). Des filaments parfois long de plusieurs mètres caractérisent l’espèce. Ces derniers sont constitués de cellules urticantes provoquant une douleur vive pour les êtres humains. La peau peut alors devenir rouge, gonfler et présenter des marques. Et dans les cas les plus sévères, les piqûres peuvent provoquer des maux de tête, des vertiges, des sueurs, des crampes, des vomissements et des douleurs musculaires. En mer, l’homme peut présenter des symptômes de désorientation, de quoi mettre en danger davantage les nageurs. Habituellement présente en Méditerranée et au sud de l’Atlantique, la physalie avance vers la Bretagne, où ses filaments urticants peuvent entraîner des symptômes graves chez l’homme. Marché de l’art : les maisons de ventes belges retrouvent leur souffle Une œuvre de Rembrandt lors d’une vente Sotheby’s à Londres en 2025 (photo d’illustration). - AFP. L a première surprise de 2026 est peut-être là. Après deux années d’attentisme, le marché de l’art retrouve des couleurs au moment même où peu d’observateurs l’attendaient. Christie’s annonce un chiffre d’affaires semestriel de 4,5 milliards de dollars, en hausse de 58 %, tandis que Sotheby’s atteint 4,4 milliards. Plus révélateur encore, cette embellie ne repose plus uniquement sur quelques chefs-d’œuvre millionnaires : les ventes de milieu de gamme, les enchères en ligne et les taux de vente repartent eux aussi à la hausse. La tendance se vérifie également en Belgique. « Peut-être sommes-nous les premiers surpris de l’engouement nettement marqué pour notre beau métier », reconnaît Dominique de Villegas, directeur de l’hôtel de ventes Horta. Malgré les tensions géopolitiques et les incertitudes économiques, la maison observe une fréquentation en hausse, aussi bien dans la salle que sur internet. Peut-être sommes-nous les premiers surpris de l’engouement nettement marqué pour notre beau métier Dominique de Villegas , Directeur de l’hôtel de ventes Horta Cette confiance retrouvée ne signifie pourtant pas que les inquiétudes économiques ont disparu. A Bruxelles, le Mont-de-Piété, établissement public spécialisé dans le prêt sur gage, en offre une illustration singulière. En 2025, le montant moyen des prêts est passé de 1.002 à 1.247 euros, tandis que la valeur moyenne des objets vendus est passée de 956 à 1.373 euros, une évolution largement portée par la hausse du cours de l’or. Le chiffre d’affaires atteint 5,46 millions d’euros, contre 4,95 millions un an plus tôt, tandis que le résultat net, à 862.823 euros, a été multiplié par plus de quatre. Pour autant, cette progression ne traduit pas, selon l’établissement, une précarisation durable, mais un recours accru à un financement ponctuel. À lire aussi Du scroll au marteau : comment Instagram et TikTok redéfinissent la stratégie des maisons de vente Les prêts répondent à des besoins immédiats de trésorerie auprès d’un public de plus en plus diversifié et 98 % des objets déposés sont finalement récupérés par leurs propriétaires. Plus de 2,1 millions d’euros de bonus de vente ont par ailleurs été reversés aux déposants en 2025. Le Mont-de-Piété entend ainsi faire évoluer l’image du prêt sur gage, présenté comme une alternative au surendettement fondée sur un accompagnement personnalisé et de proximité. Le marché à l’heure du continu Cette évolution tient aussi à une transformation profonde du fonctionnement des enchères. Longtemps organisé autour d’un calendrier immuable, le marché fonctionne désormais en continu. Les plateformes numériques ont progressivement effacé la saisonnalité des ventes tout en ouvrant les maisons de ventes à une clientèle mondiale. A Horta, Dominique de Villegas attribue en grande partie cette évolution au développement de Drouot, qui a durablement accru la fréquentation, aussi bien en ligne qu’en salle. « Depuis internet, une bonne pièce peut trouver sa place en janvier, en juin ou en décembre sans que cela ne change son résultat », observe-t-il. À lire aussi Les invisibles du marché de l’art : que deviennent les œuvres que l’on ne voit plus ? Le même phénomène s’observe dans la provenance des enchérisseurs : des œuvres acquises autrefois par des voyageurs belges retrouvent aujourd’hui des amateurs dans leur pays d’origine. « Des artistes de pays fort lointains ayant été acquis par des aïeux voyageurs trouvent, toujours grâce à internet, des amateurs lointains souhaitant se réapproprier une œuvre égarée en notre plat pays. Encore une fois, le miracle de la fibre », sourit-il. Chez Arenberg Auctions, Jeroen Luyckx, spécialiste des œuvres graphiques, fait le même constat. Grâce à la diffusion simultanée sur Drouot et Invaluable, des enchérisseurs de New York à Pékin suivent désormais les ventes en direct, même si la clientèle demeure majoritairement européenne. La revanche de la provenance Cette internationalisation ne signifie pourtant pas que tout se vende. Au contraire, les professionnels décrivent un marché devenu plus exigeant. Pour Jeroen Luyckx, « la qualité de l’œuvre, la réputation de l’artiste, son état de conservation et sa provenance déterminent la valeur ». Les œuvres anonymes trouvent plus difficilement preneur, tandis que les défauts de conservation pèsent davantage qu’auparavant sur les adjudications. Cette sélectivité rejoint d’ailleurs la stratégie revendiquée par Christie’s, qui privilégie désormais des estimations plus prudentes afin de stimuler la concurrence entre les enchérisseurs. À lire aussi Le curieux marché des archives, entre trésors historiques et documents du quotidien Les adjudications les plus marquantes de ce premier semestre illustrent parfaitement cette nouvelle prudence. Chez Arenberg, un ouvrage consacré aux costumes des Ballets russes, estimé seulement 150 euros, s’est envolé à 10.000 euros. Une photographie de Fernand Khnopff a dépassé les 13.000 euros pour une estimation de 1.500 euros, tandis qu’un manuscrit médical anversois du début du XVIIᵉ siècle a largement dépassé son estimation. Le constat vaut également pour la bande dessinée. Début juin, AZ Auction a établi un nouveau record mondial pour une planche originale de Gaston Lagaffe. Provenant de la collection de l’ancienne secrétaire d’André Franquin, à qui le dessinateur l’avait offerte, elle était estimée entre 40.000 et 50.000 euros avant d’être adjugée 160.000 euros. Une envolée qui rappelle combien la provenance et l’histoire d’une œuvre peuvent aujourd’hui démultiplier sa valeur. La vacation du 7 juin a totalisé 880.000 euros et enregistré un taux de vente de 93 %, confirmant le dynamisme du marché belge de la bande dessinée de collection. Le nouvel équilibre du marché Plus qu’un simple rebond, le premier semestre 2026 révèle peut-être une transformation plus profonde. Dans un marché ancien, où les chefs-d’œuvre véritablement inédits se font rares, la création de valeur repose de plus en plus sur la remise en circulation des œuvres. Successions, arbitrages de collections, redécouvertes, provenances documentées ou retour d’objets vers leur pays d’origine alimentent désormais une dynamique où l’histoire d’une œuvre compte parfois autant que sa qualité intrinsèque. Les records enregistrés cette année racontent moins une flambée spéculative qu’une intensification des échanges. Dominique de Villegas entrevoit la suite avec une confiance prudente. « Le bilan semestriel est donc positif, malgré la situation, ce qui nous pousse à être optimistes pour 2027, les mid-terms ne nous faisant plus autant trembler. » À lire aussi Comment le certificat d’authenticité façonne le marché des œuvres Le marché de l’art ne retrouve donc pas simplement son souffle. Il change progressivement de moteur. Plus international, plus numérique et plus sélectif, il semble désormais porté moins par la recherche du record que par une circulation renouvelée des œuvres, des collectionneurs et des capitaux. Malgré une économie mondiale sous tension, les maisons de ventes signent un premier semestre inattendu. Au-delà des records, 2026 révèle un marché plus international, plus sélectif et porté par une confiance retrouvée, sans dissiper la prudence. Par Soline Heurtebise Le 3/08/2026 à 11:12

J auge de l’impact de la réforme du chômage, le dernier bilan mensuel de l’administration de l’intégration sociale est tombé. Il concerne les statistiques des personnes qui, exclues du droit aux allocations de chômage ou d’insertion, ont obtenu le revenu d’intégration sociale. Voici la photographie de la situation, pour la période allant de début janvier à fin juin. A l’échelle du pays, 87.788 personnes ont été privées d’allocations de chômage et 11.356 d’allocations d’insertion. Et elles sont respectivement 45 % et 36,4 % à obtenir un revenu d’intégration. Réunies, ces deux catégories représentent un report vers les CPAS de 44 %. La Flandre moins impactée Au niveau régional, sans surprise, la Flandre, moins touchée par la réforme, se situe toujours en deçà : 34,3 % des exclus ont abouti dans un CPAS. A Bruxelles, ce pourcentage monte à 43,9 %. La Wallonie et la communauté germanophone sont davantage impactées, avec respectivement un taux de bascule de 48,6 et 55,1 %. Ces résultats dépassent pour l’instant les estimations de l’Arizona selon lesquelles un tiers des exclus retrouverait un emploi ; un autre tiers se tournerait vers les CPAS ; et le dernier tiers sortirait des radars pour se tourner vers la solidarité familiale, l’épargne privée ou la débrouille. Et cela avant le bilan d’une vague d’exclusion importante entamée au 1 er juillet dernier. Deux géants pharmaceutiques envisagent une fusion à 400 milliards de dollars L e géant pharmaceutique britannique AstraZeneca et son rival américain Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) ont tenu des discussions sur une éventuelle fusion, qui donnerait naissance à l’un des plus grands laboratoires au monde valorisé près de 400 milliards de dollars, selon le Financial Times . La nouvelle faisait dévisser le titre d’AstraZeneca de quelque 7 % peu après l’ouverture de la Bourse de Londres lundi. Contacté par l’AFP, le laboratoire britannique n’a pas souhaité faire de commentaire. Les deux groupes « ont mené des discussions en vue d’un rapprochement ces derniers mois », indique le quotidien économique dans un article paru dimanche soir, citant des personnes proches du dossier, pour qui « les pourparlers pourraient aboutir à un accord dans un avenir proche, mais pourraient également être retardés ou échouer ». AstraZeneca est valorisé environ 196 milliards de livres à la Bourse de Londres (selon des chiffres qui précèdent l’ouverture des échanges lundi) soit environ 264 milliards de dollars. BMS affiche de son côté une valorisation boursière de 133 milliards de dollars. Le géant pharmaceutique britannique AstraZeneca a publié la semaine dernière un bénéfice net en hausse de plus de 2 % au deuxième trimestre, à 2,5 milliards de dollars, continuant de bénéficier des ventes de ses traitements contre le cancer. Le britannique, qui espère que les États-Unis compteront pour la moitié de son chiffre d’affaires d’ici 2030, avait dévoilé il y a un an un plan d’investissement de 50 milliards de dollars dans ce pays d’ici à cette échéance. Autre signe de son rapprochement avec les États-Unis, le laboratoire est coté depuis le 2 février à la Bourse de New York, mais conserve cependant sa cotation principale à la Bourse de Londres. BMS a publié de son côté la semaine dernière un bénéfice net plus que doublé au deuxième trimestre, à 3,3 milliards de dollars, tiré notamment par ses médicaments contre le cancer (Opdivo Qvantig), l’anémie (Reblozyl) ou les maladies cardiovasculaires (Camzyos). AstraZeneca et Bristol Myers Squibb ont engagé des discussions en vue d’une possible fusion, qui pourrait donner naissance à un géant pharmaceutique valorisé près de 400 milliards de dollars, selon le Financial Times. Phoebe Bridgers, du trauma à l’hymne folk-rock Phoebe Bridgers en live : immersion totale et solidarité ! Alors qu’à Forest National aussi les téléphones seront bannis, pour vivre l’expérience à 100 %, chaque ticket vendu permettra de reverser 1 euro à l’association PLUS1 qui lutte contre les violences sexuelles. E n 2020, pour les BBC Radio 1 Piano Sessions, Phoebe Bridgers et Arlo Parks transforment l’emblématique Fake plastic trees de Radiohead en un bijou d’émotion pure. Dans une église londonienne, les deux artistes nous en offrent une version piano-voix d’un dépouillement absolu. Pendant que la première caresse les touches avec délicatesse, la seconde, dans sa tenue noire floquée d’un grand squelette, chante, à fleur de peau, d’une fragilité bouleversante. Leurs voix s’entrelacent sur les refrains, sublimant la mélancolie de Thom Yorke. Plus qu’une simple reprise, c’est une performance habitée qui donne des frissons, belle à pleurer ! Confirmant le statut de Phoebe Bridgers : une pure anomalie pop. Silhouette gracile, look de squelette, cheveux d’un blanc polaire et regard hanté : l’Américaine, qui fêtera ses 32 ans dans une dizaine de jours, est devenue la référence absolue d’une génération désabusée. Son truc ? Convertir la dépression clinique, l’apocalypse et les traumas intimes en hymnes folk-rock d’une beauté désarmante. Avec un sens aigu du détail et de l’humour noir. Mais qu’on ne s’y trompe pas : sa tristesse est un outil de travail, pas un trait de caractère. « Ecrire des chansons tristes ne signifie pas que je suis une personne triste », confiait-elle à American Songwriter . La musique lui sert de soupape de sécurité, pour extirper ce qui grouille tout au fond : « Beaucoup de mes amis proches sont musiciens et consumés par l’idée de la mort. Leurs têtes sont comme des chambres de torture. » Orfèvre du quotidien Née à Pasadena, en Californie, Phoebe Bridgers grandit modestement et trouve son refuge dans l’écriture. Son génie réside dans un sens aigu du détail banal et de la punchline assassine. Sur l’album Punisher (2020), elle chante l’angoisse moderne d’une jeunesse scotchée à ses écrans, naviguant entre crise climatique et ruptures. « I swear I’m not angry, that’s just my face », s’amuse-t-elle dans Kyoto , en évoquant le « resting bitch face » : ce visage naturellement fermé ou sévère au repos, alors qu’il s’agit simplement de l’expression neutre de quelqu’un qui n’est ni triste ni en colère… Insatiable perfectionniste, elle décrivait pour Musixmatch son obsession du mot juste et l’effet magique lorsqu’un collaborateur « remplace un seul mot qui a la même phonétique, mais qui soudainement lie toute la chanson ». Cet artisanat brut l’a aussi menée à des collaborations majeures, que ce soit avec SZA ou Taylor Swift. Mais cette quête d’excellence explose surtout avec Boygenius, le supergroupe féministe et queer formé avec ses copines Julien Baker et Lucy Dacus. Ensemble, elles bousculent l’industrie (trois Grammy Awards en 2024 pour The record ) et transforment leur sororité en force créative. Elles sont tellement inséparables que Julien et Lucy chantent sur son prochain album, Lost Weekend . Entre parenthèses : on est bien désolés, mais on ne pourra vous parler de ce nouveau disque avant le jour de sa sortie, le 14 août, le label ayant décidé de l’enfermer jusque-là dans un coffre-fort ! La pochette du prochain album « Lost Weekend », premier album solo de Phoebe Bridgers depuis six ans, qui sortira le 14 août prochain. - D.R. Paradoxe de l’authenticité Naviguer dans la célébrité à l’ère des réseaux sociaux est un exercice d’équilibriste qu’elle observe avec détachement. Pour Interview Magazine , Phoebe Bridgers s’interrogeait sur la récupération commerciale du spleen : « Tu passes ton temps à essayer de vendre un matelas de manière nonchalante, à vendre ta voix détachée à une entreprise qui achète ton authenticité. » Elle confiait aussi au magazine Russh son désir de protection : « Si je pouvais changer quelque chose, j’aimerais que les gens en sachent moins sur moi. » Malgré ce souhait, ses fans continuent de chercher leurs propres vérités dans ses failles. Qu’elle hurle à pleins poumons en fin de concert, chemisier ouvert, ou murmure des secrets à des millions d’auditeurs, elle reste la prophétesse d’une époque qui a appris à danser sur les décombres. Une artiste rare qui regarde le vide en face. Et y trouve des univers. Phoebe Bridgers en concert le samedi 5 décembre à Forest National (sold out) Six ans après « Punisher », opus confiné couronné de nominations aux Grammys, Phoebe Bridgers signe son retour. Rendez-vous ce 14 août dans les bacs pour découvrir « Lost weekend », son troisième album studio. Portrait d’une icône queer et féministe au spleen salvateur. Par Didier Stiers Le 3/08/2026 à 11:38

الصين ترسم خطوطا حمراء للدفاع عن نموذجها الاقتصادي. أكدت الصين تمسكها بنموذجها الاقتصادي القائم على دعم التصنيع والاستثمار، رافضة الضغوط الغربية لتغييره، في رسائل سبقت مفاوضات تجارية مرتقبة مع الولايات المتحدة والاتحاد الأوروبي.
البحر أمامكم... شهدت سبتة موجة نزوح غير مسبوقة من المغرب خلفت ضحايا وأثارت ردودا دولية. ويرى الكاتب أن الأزمة تكشف اختلالات اجتماعية وسياسية عميقة، ودعا إلى معالجة جذور الهجرة لا نتائجها فقط.
حرب على المقاعد الخاوية.. كومو الإيطالي يفرض قوانين صارمة على جماهيره. كشفت إدارة نادي كومو الإيطالي عن سياسة جديدة لتنظيم شؤون الجماهير، في خطوة أثارت تفاعلا واسعا قبل انطلاق الموسم الجديد.

حصار ترمب يطفئ أنوار كوبا.. 10 ملايين إنسان يغرقون في الظلام. أعلنت الشركة الوطنية للكهرباء في كوبا انقطاع التيار ليلة الاثنين في أنحاء هذا البلد الخاضع لحصار نفطي أمريكي خانق، وذلك في أعقاب ثلاثة انقطاعات تامة للتيار الكهربائي الشهر الماضي.

تفشي الحصبة في جبل مرة.. هل تنهار آخر معاقل الصحة بدارفور؟. في جبل مرة، تفتك الحصبة بالأطفال في ظل غياب اللقاحات والأطباء، بينما يدفع سوء التغذية والاكتظاظ وانهيار الخدمات الصحية المنطقة نحو كارثة أوسع مع اقتراب موسم الأمطار، ولا تلقى النداءات استجابة حتى الآن.

هل تمهد آبل لتحويل "سيري إيه آي" إلى خدمة بمقابل؟. تدرس آبل إمكانية تحويل بعض قدرات سيري المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي إلى مزايا مدفوعة ضمن آي كلاود بلس، في خطوة قد تعكس تحولا جديدا في سوق الذكاء الاصطناعي القائم على الاشتراكات.

إيران.. لا محادثات مع أمريكا حاليا ولا تغيير بهرمز في ظل الحصار. قالت إيران إنها لا تجري حاليا أي محادثات مع الولايات المتحدة، وأكدت أن الوضع في مضيق هرمز سيظل على حاله ما استمر الحصار البحري والهجمات الأمريكية.

حماية مستوطن تفجر الأزمة.. كاتس يقيل قائد القيادة الوسطى عبر التلفزيون. أعلن وزير الدفاع الإسرائيلي إقالة قائد المنطقة الوسطى آفي بالوط لإصداره عقوبات لمستوطن شارك في هجوم على فلسطينيين في مارس/آذار الماضي، مما فجر خلافا مع رئيس الأركان إيال زامير.

الين يقفز ونيكي يتراجع والمتعاملون يترقبون مزيدا من التدخل. قفز الين اليوم ‌الاثنين مما أبقى المتداولين بحالة تأهب لمزيد من التدخل من جانب السلطات اليابانية لدعم العملة التي ⁠تشهد ضعفا تاريخيا، في حين تراجع مؤشر نيكي الياياني.

عائلتها تتطلع لعلاجها بالخارج.. غارة إسرائيلية تحرق "مسك" وتفقدها السمع والنطق. أدى قصف إسرائيلي في ديسمبر/كانون الأول الماضي إلى تناثر نيران موقد العائلة، فأصاب الطفلة مسك بحروق شديدة. ومع حر الصيف وقلة العلاج، تزيد معاناة الطفلة وعائلتها التي تتطلع إلى السفر لعلاجها في الخارج.

سبتة ومليلية ليستا وحدهما.. أراض وجزر أفريقية ما زالت خاضعة لأوروبا. أعادت موجة العبور الجماعي التي شهدتها مدينة سبتة الأسبوع الماضي ملف الأراضي والجزر الأفريقية التي ما زالت تسيطر عليها أوروبا إلى صدارة الاهتمام.

ممنوع استخدام الهواتف.. والدة مبابي تفرض قوانين صارمة على شباب كاين. منعت فايزة العماري، والدة كيليان مبابي، استخدام الهواتف المحمولة داخل مقر تدريبات نادي كاين، بهدف فرض الانضباط وتعزيز تواصل اللاعبين، وسط إشادة الإدارة.

الذهب يرتفع والنفط يتراجع بعد إرجاء ترمب شن هجوم على إيران. ارتفعت أسعار ‌الذهب اليوم مع تراجع النفط بعد أن ألغى الرئيس ⁠الأمريكي دونالد ⁠ترمب شن هجوم جديد على إيران أملا في التوصل إلى اتفاق سريع، مما خفف قليلا من المخاوف بشأن التضخم ورفع ⁠أسعار الفائدة.

إيران تعدم رجلين بتهمة التجسس لصالح إسرائيل. أعدمت إيران رجلين شنقا بتهمة التجسس لصالح إسرائيل، في أحدث حلقة من سلسلة إعدامات بتهم التجسس التي تزايدت بشكل ملحوظ منذ بدء الحرب الأمريكية الإسرائيلية عليها.

إستراتيجية ترمب المتقلبة تجاه إيران بين ضغط الحلفاء والحسابات الانتخابية. اعتمد الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترمب في الحرب على إيران منذ 5 أشهر سياسة تهديد بضربات واسعة ثم تراجع تحت ضغط الحلفاء والخشية الانتخابية، فيما يشكك خصومه بجدوى نهجه المتقلب وقدرته على إخضاع طهران.

البداية من الصفر.. مزارعو غزة يحاولون إحياء أراضيهم المدمرة. يحاول مزارعون في قطاع غزة إعادة استصلاح أراضيهم التي دمرتها الحرب الإسرائيلية، رغم الخسائر الكبيرة التي لحقت بالأشجار والبنية الزراعية وارتفاع تكاليف الإنتاج وشح مستلزمات الزراعة.
"المشروع المنتظر".. أرتيتا يقود محاولات أرسنال خطف فينيسيوس. يكثف أرسنال مساعيه للتعاقد مع فينيسيوس جونيور، ويقود أرتيتا المفاوضات فنيا، في انتظار اجتماع اللاعب مع إدارة ريال مدريد لحسم مستقبله.
عمر لطفي باشا.. كيف تحول ضابط هارب من النمسا إلى قائد جيوش العثمانيين؟. من ضابط نمساوي هارب إلى منصب القائد الأعلى للجيش العثماني، سطر عمر لطفي باشا سيرة ملحمية.

حين يكون الصف السادس سقف أحلام الفتيات.. كيف ترد طالبان؟. قالت هيومن رايتس ووتش إن طالبان تفكك حقوق النساء وتمنع تعليم الفتيات بعد الصف السادس وتضيّق على الإعلام، بينما ترد الحركة بأن قراراتها تستند إلى الشريعة والتقاليد وبأن التعليق مؤقت.

زلزال جديد في مصر.. لماذا لا يهدأ خليج السويس؟. عزا خبير تكرار الزلازل المرتبطة بمنطقة خليج السويس إلى أنه جزء من منظومة جيولوجية عملاقة تشكلت مع انفتاح البحر الأحمر قبل نحو 20 إلى 30 مليون سنة، ولا تزال الصدوع المرتبطة بهذه المنظومة نشطة حتى اليوم.

Palestinian ‘doctor of the poor’ says he faces abuse, medical neglect in Israeli prison Submitted by Bilge Kotan on Sun, 08/02/2026 - 19:37 The 71-year-old physician, well known for providing care to low-income Palestinians, was arrested in the occupied West Bank in June News of Rantisi’s detention prompted widespread condemnation (Screengrab/X/@Mistaclim) Off Dr Mazen Rantisi, a 71-year-old Palestinian physician popularly described as the “doctor of the poor”, says he has suffered physical abuse and medical neglect since Israeli authorities detained him more than a month ago, Haaretz reported on Sunday. The doctor, known for often waiving fees, supplying medicines and operating a clinic that serves as a refuge for low-income Palestinians, was detained in a pre-dawn raid on his home in Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on 21 June. Prosecutors later indicted him for serving as chairman of the board of the Union of Health Work Committees, a Palestinian non-profit that provides medical care to thousands of Palestinians each year. According to the report, Rantisi told a lawyer from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel that prison authorities withheld his regular medication for the first 10 days in Ofer prison and are still denying him one of his medicines. His requests to see a doctor went unanswered, and a medic checked his pulse only once through a small opening in the cell door. Rantisi also reported physical violence, saying that said the prison units raided his cell several times a week and beat detainees. “The younger prisoners surround me to protect me, taking the beatings themselves,” Rantisi said, adding that the guards sprayed tear gas into the cell during one raid, leaving him struggling to breathe. Saja Mishraki-Baransa, the first lawyer to see Rantisi face to face since his arrest, said the physician has rapidly lost weight after receiving tiny portions of food that he described as unfit for human consumption, including mouldy bread, almost-rotten tomatoes, uncooked hummus and foul-smelling rice. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); He also said ten prisoners share his six-bed cell, with four taking turns sleeping on mattresses on the floor. The Israel Prison Service rejected the physician’s account, saying that it held all prisoners in accordance with the law, the Haaretz report said. The physician’s account, however, echoes accounts from other Palestinian detainees and prisoners. Why Israel is a friend of budding autocrats around the world Submitted by Antony Loewenstein on Wed, 07/29/2026 - 21:27 As global public opinion turns against Tel Aviv, the Netanyahu regime is ramping up its electoral meddling, from Europe to South America Presidential hopeful Flavio Bolsonaro appears with his wife, Fernanda, during the launch of his candidacy in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on 25 July 2026 (Nelson Almeida/AFP) On I have spent more than a decade investigating the Israeli arms and surveillance industries, and have always understood that the Israeli state is far more involved than it publicly admits. The revolving door between the public and private sector is well-known , but how exactly did some of the biggest Israeli companies achieve such incredible access to governments around the world, from Saudi Arabia to Ethiopia? Beyond Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s spyware diplomacy - a highly effective way to make friends, by offering sophisticated tools to spy on perceived enemies, journalists, human rights workers and even friends - there were always gaps in our knowledge. But a recent revelation provides a window into how it happened. In 2013, Shalev Hulio - one of the founders of NSO Group, which developed the phone spyware Pegasus - travelled to Panama on an Israeli diplomatic passport and stayed at the Israeli embassy. The vital reporting by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project and two other media outlets found that Hulio was central to NSO Group’s sale of Pegasus to Panama in 2012, and that he signed the contract with the Panamanian government. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); “Panamanian migration records obtained by reporters show Hulio arrived at Tocumen airport in Panama City from the U.S. on a Copa Airlines flight on December 3, 2013, and used a diplomatic passport to enter the country. The records state Hulio’s visit was for ‘recreation’ and list his profession as ‘diplomat,’” the report notes. This piece of the puzzle confirms part of a story that has been hard to pin down with documents, and not just conjecture: NSO Group and many other Israeli arms and surveillance firms operate as an arm of the Israeli state, advancing its interests, biases and agendas - and operating with its full protection. Political leverage The vast treasure trove of information that has been gathered by NSO Group and other like-minded firms is incalculable, as they are the ones extracting data from mobile phones (as opposed to the paying clients). It’s thus inevitable that NSO Group, and by extension the Israeli government, have gathered information and secrets that could be used for political leverage on any number of countries. This is one way that Israel maintains such significant diplomatic leverage. The story about spyware and hacking battles over the last decade, and Israel’s central place within them, has not gone away. Israeli spying tools continue to be used against unsuspecting politicians, journalists and activists. A rampaging Israeli government wants to make friends in the international community, as public opinion turns against it in an unprecedented way From the European Parliament to Russia , the lack of regulation in the industry has allowed it to metastasize without restraint. But the threat of cyber-tools like Pegasus seems relatively minor when compared with the explosion of Israeli election interference around the globe. From Scotland to France , and Colombia to Honduras , Israeli companies are deploying the dark arts to push for pro-Israel candidates to win. This includes massive bot farms, spreading disinformation about pro- Palestinian candidates, and manipulating social media. As with the spyware industry, the world responds with paralysis and fear. This is an issue that goes to the heart of democracy and the viability of its existence. Israeli electoral manipulation services are for sale to the highest bidder, and they’re already twisting what we know and understand about the very essence of free and fair elections. Destabilisation campaigns Take Latin America, a region that’s experiencing a wave of Israeli-led disruption campaigns. Earlier this year, a story surfaced about alleged collaboration among the Trump administration, the Netanyahu regime, and former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernandez, who was sentenced in the US in 2024 on massive drug-related charges - and pardoned the following year. The plan? Destabilise “unfriendly” governments and aim to install pro-Israel and pro-US elements to undermine left-wingers, from Colombia to Mexico (the former campaign has already been successful, with the recent win of president-elect Abelardo de la Espriella). Brazil may be next, with presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro - son of the previous president, Jair Bolsonaro - launching his campaign with an endorsement from Netanyahu. How Israel sabotages democracy in the Middle East Read More » It’s fair to presume that Israeli electoral hackers will be working night and day to assist the Bolsonaro campaign and sabotage Brazilian President Luiz ‌Inacio Lula da Silva in the run-up to the October general election. Honduras once again appears to be a central point around which Israeli and American far-right pressures are being applied; the country is reportedly willing to give control of military bases and special economic zones to Israel and the US. All of this is occurring while Israel is experiencing its biggest collapse in support in its history. This is a historic change - one that could well impact western politics in the coming years. But right now, Palestine is being trampled and erased, from Gaza to the occupied West Bank . It’s hard to convey the scale of the displacement, violence and fear among Palestinians. This is the Israeli state on steroids, sensing a once-in-a-generation opportunity to remove as many Palestinians from their land as possible, making way for a truly Jewish supremacist and rabbinical state. In this context, it makes sense that a rampaging Israeli government wants to make friends in the international community, as public opinion turns against it in an unprecedented way. Electoral manipulation might seem like a desperate move from a nation on the edge, but in reality it represents an acceleration of Israel as a reliable, autocratic ally - one that proudly discriminates against minorities and Palestinians, and inspires the surging far right in the process. Refugee Convention at 75: Britain owes Palestine an answer Submitted by Victor Kattan on Wed, 07/29/2026 - 16:39 Ten months after a 400-page legal petition demanded an apology for the Balfour Declaration and its aftermath, Downing Street has said nothing A protester holds a placard during the Nakba 78 march in London, on 16 May 2026 (Loredana Sangiuliano/SOPA Images via Reuters Connect) Off Tuesday 28 July marked 75 years since the 1951 Refugee Convention was adopted at a United Nations conference in Geneva, with Britain among the states that negotiated and shaped it. The anniversary raises a question for the British government: whether it has ever confronted its role in creating the world's longest-standing refugee crisis . The occasion carries an uncomfortable irony. That same convention ultimately left Palestinian refugees - the population whose displacement was shaped in significant part by British policy - outside its ordinary protection through a separate legal regime. I have spent a large part of my career studying how international law shaped Palestine, from the origins of the conflict to the rights of its refugees. One principle runs through all of it: legal obligations do not lapse because they become inconvenient. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); This is at the heart of the Britain Owes Palestine petition, a 400-page legal submission I co-authored, which argues that Britain acted unlawfully in Palestine between 1917 and 1948, and that the UK now has a duty to formally acknowledge and apologise for that record. Through the Balfour Declaration , Britain promised to support a national home for one people on land inhabited by another, without the consent of the majority who lived there. For three decades, it governed under irreconcilable obligations, entrenching division and suppressing Palestinian self-government - at times through emergency powers that made collective punishment lawful in name while closing the courts to its victims. In 1948, Britain withdrew from the instability that its own policies had produced, leaving the population without protection. What followed was the Nakba - the "catastrophe" - in which more than 750,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled from their homes. Today, those refugees and their descendants number in the millions. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); A 'temporary' exception The Refugee Convention established a universal framework for refugee protection, overseen by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees ( UNHCR ). However, Palestinians were carved out. Because they already received assistance from the UN Relief and Works Agency ( UNRWA ), Article 1D of the convention excluded them from its scope while that assistance continued. It was conceived as a temporary arrangement, pending a political solution that was assumed to be imminent. The refugees whose displacement is most directly tied to British policy are also those least protected by the regime Britain helped create Seventy-five years later, that "temporary" arrangement still defines Palestinian refugeehood. Unrwa provides vital services, but it has no mandate to pursue the durable solutions - voluntary repatriation, local integration, resettlement - that UNHCR offers other refugee populations. As the arrangement never ended, generations of Palestinian refugees have gone without the protections that everyone else is guaranteed. The refugees whose displacement is most directly tied to British policy are also those least protected by the regime Britain helped create. This unresolved legal anomaly is one reason the petition that is now before the government matters. It asks for a search of unreleased archives, a full public response, an acknowledgement of wrongful acts, an official apology in parliament and serious consideration of reparations. Months of silence A cross-party coalition of 45 MPs and peers has urged the prime minister to respond. Some 10 months after its submission, and despite Andy Burnham replacing Keir Starmer as prime minister this month, the government has said nothing. That silence carries both legal and moral costs. Britain often invokes the Refugee Convention and international law to criticise other states and defend its own record. Yet the authority of law depends on consistent application, including to oneself. 'Gaza is a direct result of Balfour': Palestinians petition UK for reparations over historic crimes Read More » Britain cannot credibly champion refugee protection while refusing to confront its role in creating a refugee population excluded from the very regime it helped build. A state confident enough to examine its own record honestly is a state whose word on international law carries weight. Acknowledging wrongdoing can take many forms: an apology in parliament and investment in teaching a history that remains barely covered in British schools. The precedents exist: Britain has acknowledged and settled claims for colonial-era wrongs before, notably in the 2013 settlement with Kenyan victims of abuses committed during the Mau Mau uprising. The Refugee Convention was born of the conviction that displacement demands responsibility. The petition asks nothing more than Britain applying its own principles consistently. Seventy-five years after the Refugee Convention was adopted, Britain owes Palestine an answer. HEALTH: UNCOVERING WHY BABIES DIE. Field teams actively track children under five years of age every three months to closely observe health trajectories and vital events. Expectant mothers within the target areas are systematically registered and followed up with | AKU & CHAMPS programme At first glance, the Changan Karvaan parked outside one of Aga Khan University’s (AKU) field sites in Karachi’s Bhains Colony looks like an ordinary white minivan. Boxy, tinted windows, no markings to set it apart. It’s only when you get in that the disinfectant and medical equipment give it away. Under the bright clinical lights, you will find surgical gloves, syringes, tissue covers… everything needed to perform MITS, or minimally invasive tissue sampling, on even the smallest of babies in the localities of Ali Akbar Shah, Ibrahim Hyderi and Bhains Colony. This unusual approach to forensics has helped researchers paint one of the clearest pictures yet of why these babies die before their fifth birthday. In three of Karachi’s poorest neighbourhoods, a minimally invasive autopsy technique is doing what verbal accounts and hospital records couldn’t: naming the exact cause of death in babies before age five WHAT IS MITS In 2015, the Gates Foundation launched the Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance (CHAMPS) programme to better understand why babies and young children die in poor countries. It was coordinated by University of Texas, Southwestern Medical Centre and aimed to combine clinical records, laboratory testing, verbal autopsies and, where families consent, MITS, to pinpoint the biological causes of stillbirths and deaths among children under five. MITS is a post-mortem exam in which tiny amounts of tissue and fluid from key organs are taken using fine needles. These samples are analysed for pathogens, infectious disease and malignant tumours. The results reveal the exact cause of death without a full surgical autopsy. The goal is to arm governments and health agencies with evidence, so they can tackle preventable child deaths. “Children die because of certain reasons — there’s intrauterine deaths, which are before birth,” says Dr Asim Beg, parasitologist at AKU who specialises in vector-borne diseases. “The real cause for those is also more speculative because, in Pakistan, a Muslim country, they don’t do post-mortems normally,” he tells Eos. The study operates across nine countries on two continents, but Pakistan posed an obstacle unique to it: a widespread religious conviction that invasive sampling would disrespect the dead. It took at least 28 fatwas [religious edicts], countless meetings and debates with local leaders, and deep community involvement before families started to consent. “When the surveillance team first approached families, the response was overwhelmingly negative,” says Sajid Abbas, a research manager for the study. “At least 60 to 70 per cent of households refused outright.” The data collected from a MITS sample is just as comprehensive as what you’d get from a full open autopsy, according to Dr Momin Kazi, the study’s lead researcher. Tissue is collected from the brain, heart, lungs and kidneys, and, for stillbirths, the placenta is taken in its entirety. Organ samples are obtained through a puncture no larger than a pen’s tip, alongside cerebrospinal fluid, nasal, rectal and stool swabs, plus biometric measurements and photographs. MITS identifies the cause of death in 98 to 100 per cent of cases, researchers say, because they draw on polymerase chain reactions (PCRs), chromatography, and every other test available. That level of accuracy is possible because findings are deliberated upon by a panel of 12-13 experts, including professors, government representatives and specialists from private hospitals. They systematically eliminate possibilities to find the cause. Often, the visible symptoms were the ones already treated, but an underlying condition went undetected, with no symptoms. The sample size isn’t yet enough for policy, researchers say, but MITS has revealed unprecedented detail: exact pathogens, hidden causes beneath treated symptoms and new local strains no other method would catch. Researchers deliberately chose this stretch of Karachi’s coastline as a study site because it functions as a “mini Pakistan”, with families from all linguistic backgrounds and faiths. RACE AGAINST TIME When a stillbirth occurs or a child under five dies, burial usually happens within two to four hours — arrangements are minimal, beyond a ghusl [ritual bath] and shrouding. Many such deaths happen at home and are rarely logged with a hospital, leaving the cause unknown. The team’s challenge was to even find out about these mortalities. “It’s not as if every death comes through a hospital,” says Abbas. So the team mapped out the path a burial takes and everyone involved, at every step — a network that included religious figures who lead burial rites, shopkeepers and coffin makers, informal healthcare providers, ambulance drivers, and even nightwatchmen. “These are the people who alert us, and our team is available around the clock to respond, reach the family and seek consent for a sample,” explains Abbas. Mirzaadi is one such woman. She’s spent years as a community health worker in Bhains Colony, logging new families, marriages, births and deaths, long before CHAMPS operated in the area. When her daughter Rafiya was born at Koohi Goth Hospital two years ago, the baby hadn’t cried or urinated since birth. “She was passing discoloured fluid from her mouth,” Mirzaadi recalled. The family was told that the child’s organs were damaged. She was eventually put on a ventilator and died 12 days later. With Mirzaadi not in a state to engage, the project team quickly took consent from her husband Mushtaq, himself a senior research assistant on CHAMPS. The blood culture result following MITS indicated that Rafiya’s likely cause of death was acute gastroenteritis. It wasn’t her kidneys as initially suspected. The culprit was the qehva [green tea] that was given to the newborn. According to Dr Vinod Kumar from The Indus Hospital, common practices such as prelacteal feeding (giving any substance other than breast milk to newborn babies during their first threedays) compromise a baby’s health. “[People say] let’s give honey, or water, or qehva or unpasteurised goat milk,” he tells Eos. Any of them can lead to an infection. MITS has helped families uncover the reason for multiple child deaths. In one case, for example, a virus was detected and treated so the couple’s subsequent children survived. A child infected with Streptococcus pneumoniae, for instance, might also test positive for cytomegalovirus — these opportunistic pathogens strike children who are already sick and more vulnerable. A child placed on a ventilator who then develops ventilator-associated pneumonia, for example, points to a clear, fixable gap: infection control on the equipment itself needs to improve. LOCAL BUGS The pathogens behind neonatal sepsis in Pakistan, according to neonatologist Dr Kumar, look nothing like what doctors encounter in higher-income countries. “We majorly deal with a few of the common bacterial organisms, which include Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter, Staphylococcus aureus, and E. coli,” he says, contrasting this with the Group B Streptococcus that dominates in Western neonatal units. Most of these bugs are hospital-acquired — a consequence of overcrowded wards, thin nursing ratios, where “one nurse is looking after four or five babies, or sometimes eight”, making cross-infection almost inevitable. CHAMPS’ initial data supports this. Hospital-acquired and drug-resistant superbug infections, such as Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, occurred overwhelmingly or exclusively in hospitals, showing how drug-resistant bugs thrive in clinical wards The initial data shows a stark contrast between deaths taking place at home and those at a hospital. Measles was the leading cause of death, indicating that these children were not getting their routine immunisation. More troubling was that Streptococcus pneumoniae (six cases) occurred exclusively at home — proof that fatal respiratory infections were killing children before they ever reached a hospital. Among the deaths for which parents consented to MITS, 31 percent were stillbirths, 63 percent involved infants younger than one year of age and six percent occurred among children aged one to five. Although child mortality in these coastal neighbourhoods remains alarmingly high, families now have something they previously lacked: the chance to know exactly why their child died. SSGC assures citizens there is no gas leak, says odourisation plant testing led to complaints. The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) said on Sunday that complaints of a suspected gas leak near Karachi’s Abul Hasan Isphahani Road since the previous night were due to the testing of odourisation plants during the commissioning of a new pipeline. While gas is often thought to have a distinctive smell, it is in fact odourless. Gas suppliers deliberately add odorants to the gas as a safety measure to alert consumers to potentially life-threatening leaks. In a media alert issued on Sunday, the SSGC said that odourants used to give gas its distinctive smell were added in larger quantities for testing purposes. This resulted in a stronger-than-usual smell, prompting reports of a gas leak from various parts of Karachi. “The SSGC administration wishes to make it clear that all system pressures are normal and that no gas leak of any kind has been reported,” the statement said. “The smell is solely due to the relatively larger quantity of odourants added to the gas during the testing of the odourisation plants.” The company requested its customers to remain calm and continue their regular activities. Gas leaks can be life-threatening, causing explosions and fires as well as death by suffocation. In January, three women suffocated to death, while another fainted in a gas leak incident in an apartment in Rawalpindi’s Bahria Town Phase VII.

Electoral rolls shrink by 589,458 in less than two months as ECP removes 1.48m deceased voters. ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s electoral rolls contracted by 589,458 voters between May 7 and July 2, 2026, as the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) removed a large number of deceased voters from the electoral database, more than offsetting fresh registrations during the period, it emerged on Sunday. According to official ECP statistics analysed by Dawn , the total number of registered voters fell from 137,163,857 on May 7 to 136,574,399 on July 2. A senior ECP official said 895,000 new voters were enrolled during the period, but the deletion of around 1.48 million deceased voters resulted in a net decline of 589,458 voters nationwide. The number of male voters dropped from 73,286,821 to 72,835,859, a decrease of 450,962, while female voters declined from 63,877,036 to 63,738,540, down by 138,496. The reduction narrowed the gender gap among registered voters from about 941,000 to 910,000. Overall, 99 of the country’s 144 districts recorded a decline in registered voters, while 45 districts posted a net increase. Punjab Punjab accounted for the overwhelming share of the decline. The province lost 478,909 voters, with the total falling from 77,955,543 to 77,476,634, representing 81.2 per cent of the nationwide reduction. Nine of the 10 districts with the largest declines were in Punjab. According to ECP figures, Faisalabad recorded the largest decrease, with 41,264 voter entries removed, bringing the district’s total down from 56,18,044 to 55,76,780. It was followed by Sheikhupura, with a decline of 31,783 voters, from 22,68,275 to 22,36,492; Gujranwala, with a drop of 30,302 voters, from 29,79,820 to 29,49,518; and Sialkot, which lost 30,129 voters, bringing the number down from 29,84,882 to 29,54,753. The number of voters in Gujrat dropped by 29,553, followed by Sargodha with a decline of 26,675, Multan with 26,420, Kasur with 24,367 and Bahawalpur with 22,259. Likewise, Khanewal saw a decline of 19,504 voters, Rahim Yar Khan 18,574, Lahore 16,633, Narowal 15,914, Toba Tek Singh 15,395, Rawalpindi 13,577, Mandi Bahauddin 13,480 and Attock 11,180. The number of voters in Nankana Sahib and Muzaffargarh declined by over 10,000 each. Another nine districts saw a decrease of over 5,000 each. These included Okara, which saw a decline of 9,784 voters; Khushab, 8,226; Chakwal, 7,377; Dera Ghazi Khan, 6,755; Wazirabad, 6,723; Rajanpur, 6,621; Kot Addu, 6,358; Lodhran, 6,348; and Chiniot, 5,396. Sindh Sindh recorded the second-largest provincial decline, losing 97,216 voters, with the total dropping from 28,772,963 to 28,675,747. Karachi South recorded the largest decline in the province, with 20,243 fewer voters, making it the only non-Punjab district among the top 10 districts with the biggest declines. The number of voters in the district fell from 13,30,682 to 13,10,439. It was followed by Karachi East, where the removal of 16,873 voters brought the total down from 18,15,780 to 17,98,907. Keamari lost 9,983 voters, Karachi West 8,394, Hyderabad 7,573, Khairpur 7,228 and Sanghar 6,240. KP Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) recorded a comparatively small net decline of 9,046 voters, with the provincial total falling from 23,415,995 to 23,406,949. However, it was the only province where more districts recorded gains than losses. In overall terms, the province lost 9,049 voters, accounting for 1.53 per cent of the total decline. While the number of male voters slipped by 16,884, the number of female voters increased by 7,838. Haripur lost 4,978 votes, followed by Abbottabad with 4,182, Charsadda with 3,946, Kohat with 3,352, Nowshera with 3,313, Lower Dir with 3,153 and DI Khan with 2,895. Other districts to have lost over 2,000 votes included Mardan, Hangu and Bannu. Balochistan In Balochistan, the number of voters declined by 2,226, accounting for a 0.38pc decrease. The total fell from 57,65,008 to 57,62,782, reducing the number of male voters by 6,518 while increasing the number of female voters by 4,292. Loralai and Sibi saw declines of 1,048 and 1,025, respectively. Most districts recorded marginal changes, restricted to two or three digits. Islamabad Capital Territory saw a small decline of 2,061 voters, from 12,54,348 to 12,52,287. Those removed from the electoral rolls comprised 1,118 men and 940 women. Despite the overall decline, 45 districts recorded an increase in registered voters between May 7 and July 2. KP led the gains, with 20 of its 36 districts adding voters. Of Balochistan’s 36 districts, 13 saw an increase, while nine of Sindh’s 30 districts recorded a rise in voter numbers. In Punjab, only three of the province’s 41 districts witnessed an increase in the voter count. In KP, the biggest increase was recorded in Peshawar, which added 4,835 voters, taking the total from 22,46,457 to 22,51,292. Other major gains in the province included Bajaur with 3,797, Lower Dir with 3,153, Buner with 1,738 and Mansehra with 1,603. Other districts with increases of over 1,000 included Malakand, Khyber and South Waziristan (Lower). In Balochistan, Quetta remained ahead with an increase of 4,052 voters, followed by Pishin, which saw an addition of 2,523 voters. In 11 other districts, the increase ranged between 65 and 573. Sindh also saw growth in nine districts. Karachi Central recorded the highest increase in the province, with 4,428 new voters, rising from 22,60,158 to 22,64,586. Jacobabad gained 3,928 voters, Ghotki 2,479, Naushahro Feroze 2,103 and Korangi 1,024. Other districts with nominal growth included Larkana, Malir, Tharparkar and Thatta. In Punjab, only three districts saw gains, which were offset by much larger deletions elsewhere. The largest increase was recorded in Bahawalnagar, where the number of voters surged by 16,094, from 20,12,083 in May to 20,28,177 in July, followed by Sahiwal with 4,755 and Vehari with 1,089.

At least 72 died in Spain's Ceuta migrant rush. At least 72 people died during the mass influx in recent days of migrants into Spain’s Ceuta enclave, when tens of thousands of people mostly swam around the border post from Morocco, local officials said on Sunday. Most of the estimated 60,000 people who rushed into Spain’s north African territory have returned to Morocco since the territory’s largest mass migrant crossing. “The latest figure that we have is 72,” the government’s delegate to Ceuta, Miguel Angel Perez Triano, told reporters, when asked about the number of fatalities. The previous toll was 67 deaths. Spanish police and troops patrolled the streets of Ceuta on Sunday as the enclave largely returned to normal after the sudden mass influx of migrants from Morocco that had occurred between Wednesday and Friday. Only small groups of migrants were still walking around after most who crossed the small border barrier returned voluntarily to Morocco in 48 hours. AFP on Saturday saw migrant minors milling around in a disused industrial park in Ceuta. Others were seen dozing on the pavements outside. “All the children here want to go to (mainland) Spain,” said one of the few adults at the site, Moroccan man Aziz Dabch, 41. The largest migrant rush into the enclave has caused an international crisis for Spain, with European partners criticising Madrid for its immigration policies. Outside a housing project near Ceuta port, Spanish soldiers detained a group of nine tired-looking migrants who were sitting on the pavement, guarded by troops with an armoured car, an AFP reporter said. Small inflatable boats from a rescue unit scoured the waters around the border barrier that extends into the Mediterranean Sea, where a new 500-metre (1,640-feet) floating boom reinforced security. Civil Guard were also taking migrants off a bus to escort them back to the border post to return to Morocco. The border crossing was calm, with groups of workers picking up trash, clothes and rubbish left behind during the mass crossing. Rumours Spain has blamed criminal gangs for spreading rumours that a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on immigration would allow migrants easier passage. Some analysts suggested Morocco could allow migrants to cross the border to put diplomatic pressure on Spain, which has recently improved ties with Rabat’s arch-enemy neighbouring Algeria. In 2021, around 10,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta, taking advantage of Morocco easing border controls as a way to pressure Spain. Moroccan officials have so far not offered any statement on the crisis. But some of those who crossed the border said they had heard the border was open — a rumour quickly amplified on social media. The EU said it would hold a video call on Tuesday after 22 bloc members issued a joint open letter calling for an urgent meeting to agree a speedy coordinated response, and to prevent further uncontrolled crossings. Italy on Saturday implemented a one-month suspension of its Schengen agreement with Spain allowing for visa-free movement between borders. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, in a letter to EU leaders, blasted the “selfish” reaction by some EU countries. Pope Leo XIV on Sunday spoke to the situation in Ceuta in his daily prayers on Sunday, saying he was following it “with concern” and hoping for a solution of “peace, stability and justice”.

At least 14 people, including police officials, martyred in suicide attack on Kabal police station in Swat: police. At least 14 people, including police officials, were martyred and at least 18 others injured in a suicide attack on Swat’s Kabal police station on Sunday, police and rescue officials said. Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi, while speaking to Dawn , confirmed the death toll. Malakand Division Deputy Inspector General of Police Fida Hussain told AFP that police officers were among those martyred. He added that another body, suspected to be that of the bomber, had been brought to the hospital. According to the Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Umar Khan, the suicide bomber detonated explosives after police personnel attempted to stop and search him at the entrance of the police station. The DPO said that the police remained on high alert. “Security forces have cordoned off the area, and an investigation is underway to collect further evidence,“ he added. The explosion occurred near the gate of Kabal police station while hundreds of people were participating in a public demonstration at nearby Kabal Chowk against the recent wave of terrorism in Swat Valley. Police officials inspect the site following a suicide bombing during a protest in Swat district on August 2. — AFP The bodies of nine victims were shifted to Central Hospital Saidu Sharif, while the bodies of five others were moved to Kabal Hospital, where doctors confirmed their deaths, said Rescue 1122 Spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi. The spokesperson added that two of the injured are reported to be in critical condition. The powerful blast caused multiple casualties, prompting an immediate emergency response from police, rescue teams and local authorities. Security personnel also sealed off the area and launched a search operation. The protest had drawn a large crowd from across the district and the attack occurred as the final speaker was addressing the crowd, triggering panic among participants. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Addressing the gathering before the blast, the speakers condemned the resurgence of terrorism in Swat and demanded that the government ensure lasting peace. They said their movement had a single agenda: the restoration of peace and the elimination of terrorism from the region. The speakers stressed that maintaining law and order and eradicating terrorism were the state’s responsibility, warning that continued insecurity could trigger widespread public unrest, citing recent protest movements in other countries as examples of growing public frustration. The speakers also criticised the authorities for what they described as action against peaceful citizens while terrorists continued to operate in the mountainous areas of Swat. They alleged that terrorists had openly circulated videos on social media and questioned why stronger action had not been taken against them. “Our children deserve education, and our families deserve to live in peace,” one speaker told the gathering. “We have witnessed years of bloodshed. Our mothers, sisters, and daughters have suffered immensely, and we do not want another generation of widows and orphans.” Condemnations pour in President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow over the loss of life and called for a comprehensive investigation into the incident, according to a statement issued by his office on X. President Zardari directed the relevant authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to those injured. “Terrorists will never succeed in their nefarious efforts to undermine peace, national unity and the writ of the state,” he was quoted as saying. He added that the sacrifices of the KP police were “a source of pride for the entire nation”. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast. “Terrorists cannot demoralise the nation with cowardly attacks,” Kundi was quoted as saying, as per a statement. KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, condemning the incident, sought a report from the KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) and offered condolences to the families of the deceased. “The elements hostile to peace will never be allowed to succeed in their nefarious intentions,” the chief minister was quoted as saying. Earlier in the day, an IED blast near the Peshawar-Islamabad motorway toll plaza injured two policemen in the provincial capital Peshawar. On July 30, a terrorist attack on a police checkpost in Hangu martyred nine policemen. KP has seen an uptick in terrorist activity. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’s monthly security assessment, KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 terrorism related deaths in July, compared with 75 in June, representing an increase of 105 per cent.

Inconsistencies in Rs332bn grid revenue flagged. ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Autho­rity member (tariff and finance) has questioned regulatory and accounting inconsistencies of the national grid’s recently-cleared revenue requirement of Rs332 billion, citing what she described as the ‘mirror image’ of receivables and non-transferred assets. Nepra member Amina Ahmed pointed out the financial inconsistencies in a detailed dissenting note on a recent 2-1 majority ruling of the regulator, approving a three-year combined revenue requirement for National Grid Company (NGC) at Rs332bn for FY2022-23, FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 for incorporation into consumer-end tariffs through use-of-system charges (UoSC) The NGC (formerly National Transmission & Despatch Company or NTDC) had sought a total of Rs478bn revenue requirement for three years under the multi-year tariff regime. This included Rs112bn for FY23, followed by 45pc rise to Rs163bn for FY24 and another 25pc rise to Rs203bn for FY25. In a majority decision issued a few days ago, Nepra allowed a total of Rs332bn revenue for three years. This included Rs81.5bn for FY23, with a 17pc increase to Rs95.6bn for FY24 and then 62pc increase to Rs155bn for FY25. As a consequence, Nepra approved UoSC at Rs382 per kiloWatt a month for FY23, Rs455 per kW for FY24 and Rs710 per kW a month for FY25. Nepra member says CPPA liability can’t be treated as loan without matching receivable However, Ms Ahmed challenged the treatment of over Rs19bn, recorded as payable to Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) under the head of current liabilities in NGC’s financial statements for 2023-24. She said the majority decision treated the amount as a loan, subtracted from the NGC’s assets to work out its equity amount. “The diminution in the equity amount has consequently resulted in a proportionate reduction in the permissible return allowed” to the NGC, she wrote. Under the business transfer agreement (BTA) of June 2015, NGC transferred the assets and liabilities pertaining to the Market Operations Undertaking to CPPA. As the carrying value of liabilities so transferred exceeded the carrying value of assets transferred, a net payable arose, representing the shortfall between the two, she said, adding the BTA has since been extended on multiple occasions and amounted to over Rs19bn as of June 30, 2024. Correspondingly, an offsetting balance was recognised under the current assets with details given in the Advances and Other Receivables, reflecting an amount recoverable by NGC from certain power sector entities. “A certain portion of these receivables represents the mirror image of the asset not transferred to CPPA,” she said, adding that had this receivable also been transferred to CPPA as part of the same BTA transaction, no such liability would have remained on NGC’s books. Separately, as per Nepra mechanism, the equity amount was to be computed by aggregating fixed assets and current assets, and then deducting the non-current and current liabilities. “The methodology does not rely upon the actual current assets and current liabilities as reported in the financial statements; instead, they are derived by applying certain prescribed formulae,” she said, arguing that while Nepra guidelines provided formula for computing current assets, the current liabilities, as per the practice, were instead taken as a fixed proportion, i.e. 2/3 of the current assets so arrived at. As a consequence, she argued that the amount due to CPPA bore no nexus whatsoever with the financing of NGC’s long-term assets. “Accordingly, this amount cannot be equated with loans (long-term) employed for financing the assets... They represent two sides of the same net position; recognising one without the other produces a distorted equity amount,” the member said. “Either both should be netted off against each other, or both excluded, selectively recognising only the liability, while ignoring its corresponding asset, is not correct,” she added. Naqvi’s call for new provinces faces fresh pushback. Defence Minister Kha­waja Asif responded to Mr Naqvi’s remarks in a post on X, in which he also referred to the DG ISPR’s comments . “Mohsin Naqvi sahib expr­essed his views on the dire state of the system. I more or less personally agree with these views,” Mr Asif wrote, describing the interior minister as a “powerhouse”. He added that, as a political worker, he believed the country’s political evolution had been “held captive to factional and personal interests for decades” and needed to be freed. The federal minister advised Mr Naqvi to begin the overhaul process by implementing NAP through his own ministry. He also urged Mr Naqvi to bring about a “revolution” in the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), which he heads in addition to serving as interior minister. Last week, Mr Naqvi had said the country’s governance system had “collapsed” and argued that Pakistan needed new administrative units, or provinces, to improve service delivery, accountability and access to justice. He also called for new leadership, saying the country’s youth wanted justice, merit and jobs rather than stipends and laptops. A day later, the military’s spokesperson also called on political parties to consider an administrative reset to improve governance, arguing that the country’s security and stability depended on adapting its governance structure to the demands of modern times and a growing population. Mr Asif said that if the system was to be str­engthened and meaningful reforms introduced, the appropriate forum was parliament, of which Mr Naqvi is a member, or the federal cabinet. “This way, these institutions and the system would be strengthened, and change would come through a constitutional process,” he said. The defence minister also pointed out that Mr Naqvi was a cabinet member but claimed he rar­ely attended parliamentary or cabinet sessions. “In my opinion, treating these institutions as irrelevant and making such a major statement before a captive audience after inviting the country’s eminent and respected businessmen does not carry the same weight that it would have had if made at the relevant constitutional forums,” he said. There is neither a prime minister, nor parliament, nor any outdated system standing in your way.” Rabbani opposes new provinces Meanwhile, former Senate chairman Mian Raza Rabbani has strongly opposed the proposal to create new provinces, arguing that Pakistan’s governance failures stem from violations of the Constitution rather than the existing federating units. Instead, he said, the real causes of the governance crisis are the erosion of provincial autonomy and the weakening of democratic institutions. According to the veteran lawmaker, several factors have contributed to the current situation. These include the repeated derailment of the democratic process, the ceding of political space to the civil-military bureaucracy, the weakening of the federation through the centralisation of powers in Islamabad, allowing dictators to amend the Constitution at will, experimenting with more than 10 models of governance since 1947, policy decisions being taken outside parliament, rendering it redundant, the failure to hold free, fair elections as envisaged, governance being carried out in blatant violation of the Constitution, disregard for the doctrine of the trichotomy of powers, the prevalence of rule by law instead of the rule of law, and the denial of provincial autonomy. “This is just the tip of the iceberg,” Mr Rabbani said. The veteran politician also proposed several measures to address the country’s governance challenges. These include strict adherence to the supremacy of the Constitution, 1973; upholding the rule of law; ensuring full compliance with the provincial autonomy guaranteed under the Constitution, 1973; strict observance of the constitutional principle of the trichotomy of powers; and devolving political, administrative, and financial authority to elected local governments as envisaged under Article 140-A of the Constitution, 1973. On the directives of Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti, the CMIT, headed by its chairman Bashir Ahmed Bangulzai, will conduct an on-site investigation into the July 30 accident. Firefighters under pressure amid raging wildfires. AGIOS KONSTANTINOS: North America and Europe have been ravaged by wildfires this summer after a period of record-breaking heatwaves and little rain conditions that scientists say have been exacerbated by climate change. In Greece, two firefighting helicopters collided while helping to control a huge wildfire on Sunday that has destroyed more than 100 homes northwest of Athens, while a fresh blaze forced evacuations on the popular tourist island of Kefalonia. Gale-force winds that had fuelled a fire around Porto Germeno on the Gulf of Corinth 60 km (40 miles) northwest of Athens subsided, but flames crossed a mountain to the south and reached the settlement of Veniza and a military firing range, igniting unexploded ordnance. Firefighters focused their efforts on preventing fire from advancing towards the coastal town of Megara, which has a population of around 30,000. In France, wildfires in the Gironde and Var departments showed signs of easing. Authorities reported only minor flare-ups in the southwestern Gironde area and said the blaze in the southeastern Var department had not spread overnight. In Monfort-Sur-Argents, in the region of Var, Georges Blanc, who fled from the fire, returned home and was busy putting out hot embers to prevent a flare-up, while firefighters watered the wider area. In central Spain, wildfires that ripped through tens of thousands of hectares over the past week were mostly under control, though firefighters were dealing with reignitions in some areas. In the western province of Caceres, a forest blaze erupted on Saturday, prompting the evacuation of around 800 people. Those residents were allowed to return on Sunday but remained confined to their homes as the fire was still active. Meanwhile, a fast-moving wildfire roared through the US city of Spokane on Saturday, forcing thousands of residents to evacuate as Washington state declared an emergency over one of its worst fire seasons on record. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson declared a state of emergency and noted that the Pacific Northwest state is enduring a fourth consecutive year of drought as climate change creates conditions propitious for destructive wildfires. Video of the wildfire shot by people driving through the city of some 230,000 on Saturday showed house after house engulfed by flames or reduced to ash as wind-fueled blazes burned out of control in hot, bone-dry weather.
