150 Manila youth hired in short‑term government jobs. A total of 150 students and out-of-school youth in Manila secured short-term jobs under the government’s Special Program for Employment of Students (SPES). The beneficiaries signed contracts on Monday through the city’s Public Employment Service Office (PESO) for an 11-day work program, giving them extra income for daily and school expenses. Manila Mayor Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso led the deployment. He said the program supports the city’s push to address basic needs such as jobs, education, housing, and healthcare. “Ang layunin natin… makapagbigay ng extra income, lalo na sa mga nag-aaral at out-of-school youth (Our goal is to provide extra income, especially for students and out-of-school youth),” he said. Vice Mayor Chi Atienza said the program expands opportunities for young Manileños. “Itong programang ito ay nagpapakita na tunay na may malasakit ang ating alkalde… importante na mabigyan ng oportunidad ang kabataan (This program shows the mayor truly cares… it is important to give opportunities to the youth),” she said. The city also cited plans to expand access to education, including a five-story building for the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila College of Medicine that could accommodate up to 5,000 students. The SPES beneficiaries were deployed with support from the city’s youth sector, alongside officials from PESO, the Manila Youth Bureau, and the SK Federation.

Mark Villar pushes for tax exemption to strengthen MSMEs, spur job creation. Senator Mark Villar has filed a measure seeking to exempt micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the Minimum Corporate Income Tax (MCIT) saying it is imperative to provide them much-needed tax relief as they serve as the key driver of the Philippine economy. Villar, in filing Senate Bill No. 2362, said MSMEs have provided significant contribution to the country yet many of them stil grapple with rising production costs, persistent inflation and other economic pressures. These challenges, he said, are further aggravated when inflation climbed to 7.2 percent in April 2026 following the declaration of a national energy emergency, leaving many MSMEs struggling to sustain their operations. “Our MSMEs are the backbone of the Philippine economy. They provide livelihood to millions of Filipinios, fuel local industries, and keep our communities economically active,” Villar said. "By giving them meaningful tax relief, we allow them to reinvest in their businesses, create more jobs, and contribute even more to our country’s development,” he added. Under the bill, Villar proposes exempting qualified MSMEs, as defined under the Magna Carta for MSMEs, from the MICT by amending the relevant provisions of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC). The bill also aims to reduce the tax burden on small businesses, enabling them to retain more capital for expansion, innovation, and job generation while improving thier competitiveness and resilience in a challenging economic environment. Villar said he hopes passage of the measure into law would give MSMEs more power to expand their operations, improve productivity, and continue driving inclusive economic growth across the country. “When our small businesses succeed, more Filipinos benefit through new jobs, stronger local economies and increased opportunities for families,” he said. “This measure is about giving our entrepreneurs the support they need to grow and helping ensure that economic progress reaches every community,” he reiterated.

Las Piñas National High School suspends face-to-face classes after fatal campus stabbing. Face-to-face classes at Las Piñas National High School (LPNHS) have been suspended for five days after the fatal stabbing of a 13-year-old student inside the campus on July 31. Principal Ignacio Son announced the suspension for junior and senior high school students from Aug. 3 to 7, citing Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 14, s. 2026, and the directive of Las Piñas City Mayor April Aguilar. The school will temporarily shift to alternative learning modalities to allow students, teachers, and personnel time for mental health and psychosocial interventions. During the suspension, students will continue lessons through printed modules, worksheets, and assignments distributed or sent via the school’s official online platforms, including Google Classroom and class group chats. Son said psychosocial processing and counseling sessions will be conducted for students, teachers, and non-teaching staff in coordination with guidance advocates, mental health professionals, and the city government. “The school remains committed to ensuring the safety, well-being, and emotional recovery of the entire school community during this difficult period,” the statement read. The administration will also review and strengthen campus security measures, including safety protocols, coordination with law enforcement, and additional preventive steps before classes resume. Aguilar directed city agencies to provide psychological support to those affected and ordered the Las Piñas City Police to heighten visibility in public schools while security measures are under review. Nearby Saint Rose of Lima School, Inc. likewise announced a temporary shift in its learning modality as a precaution. The suspension follows the fatal stabbing of a 13-year-old student by a 14-year-old classmate inside the LPNHS campus after an alleged argument. Police said the case is under investigation, and the child in conflict with the law has been placed under custody in line with the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act.

BCDA offers farms, jobs to farmers affected by Pax Silica project. The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), the state-run firm overseeing the development of the Pax Silica artificial intelligence (AI) industrial hub, said farmers affected by the project may find work opportunities in New Clark City. In a statement on Monday, Aug. 3, the BCDA said it has already designated several areas for modern agriculture projects within the 9,450-hectare (ha) New Clark City property in Capas, Tarlac, that are designed to support farmers. These areas include a 50-ha agricultural zone, the 10-ha Ayta Ethnobotanical Center, and hundreds of hectares for future agricultural development, according to the agency. The BCDA said it has also allocated relocation areas within New Clark City to minimize disruption to households affected by the project. “Together, these efforts will expand employment and strengthen sustainable livelihoods for farmers and Ayta communities in New Clark City,” the BCDA said. “As New Clark City grows, so too will opportunities for farmers and Ayta communities around it.” New Clark City is at the center of the planned development of an AI industrial hub to be developed by the United States (US) and the Philippines under the Pax Silica partnership, which aims to secure the materials necessary for the global AI supply chain. Spanning more than 1,600 ha, the project is expected to become a major investment hub for advanced manufacturing, critical mineral processing, and digital infrastructure such as data centers. While details of the plan are still being evaluated, the project is already drawing criticism over its potential impact on energy, agriculture, and the environment, as well as its potential to displace nearby communities. For one, local scientists’ group Agham said the BCDA has already issued an initial list of persons to be displaced by the project, including several farmers and indigenous peoples (IPs). Agham said the displacement, which can take the form of direct physical relocation or indirect displacement through the loss of livelihood, is expected to “undoubtedly affect the livelihoods of farmers both inside and outside the project area.” Citing reports, Senator Imee Marcos said more than 90 farmers will be displaced by the project. As such, the lawmaker has called on the BCDA to explain the project’s impact before any development can begin. In response, the BCDA said it welcomes the Senate’s oversight of the matter, noting that it stands ready to provide the facts needed for a transparent discussion. Likewise, the agency said it will meet again with Capas Mayor Roseller Rodriguez, alongside other local government units and stakeholders, to “listen, engage, and discuss the path forward together.” “BCDA remains committed to ensuring that development is inclusive, responsible, and creates lasting opportunities for every community that calls New Clark City home,” the BCDA said. BCDA President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Joshua Bingcang said last month that the AI industrial hub is expected to attract up to $70 billion worth of investments, generating around 130,000 jobs. Bingcang noted that the US and the Philippines plan to conclude contract negotiations for the project within the year, followed by the planning stage next year and construction around the first quarter of 2028.

Delay on benefits, bonuses for health workers being addressed, Palace says. Malacañang assured health workers under the Department of Health (DOH) that the issues concerning the delayed benefits and performance-based bonuses are being addressed by the Marcos administration. Although Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro noted that the delays did not happen during the term of President Marcos, but the matter is now being addressed. "Okay, noong 2021, of course, hindi pa po ito sakop ni Pangulong Marcos Jr. Pero sa ngayon po, ito po ay inaayos po (Okay, in 2021, of course, this was not yet under President Marcos Jr.'s administration. But at present, this is being addressed)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Monday, Aug. 3. According to Castro, there are only a few issues raised by the Commission on Audit (COA) while the DOH has already sent a letter to the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) seeking clarification on these matters. The issues being clarified, she added, involve the medical allowance, particularly the verification of disbursement methods—such as whether payments are made directly through HMO providers or through cash reimbursement—as well as eligibility coverage and the required supporting documents. "So, ito iyong mga issues na kinakailangang maresolba (These are the issues that still need to be resolved)," Castro said. "Pero sa mga kababayan po natin na kayo naman po talaga ay benepisyaryo, makakaasa po kayo at inaayos lamang po ang mga issues para liwanagin po ito sa DBM (To our fellow citizens who are the rightful beneficiaries, you can rest assured that you will receive your benefits. The government is simply resolving these issues and clarifying them with the DBM)," the Palace official added. In a statement, the Alliance of Health Workers said the President "failed to acknowledge the long-overdue unpaid benefits still owed to thousands of health workers," stressing that "he made no commitment to release the unpaid P7,000 Medical Allowance, the long-delayed Performance-Based Bonus (PBB) for eligible health workers for 2021, 2022, and 2024, and other pending benefits that health workers have repeatedly demanded."

ICTSI profit jumps 25% as global port expansion drives record revenue. Razon-led global port giant International Container Terminal Services Inc. (ICTSI) sustained its growth momentum in the first half despite the backdrop of the Middle East conflict, with net income rising 22 percent to nearly $590 million. Based on its regulatory disclosure on Monday, Aug. 3, ICTSI’s attributable net income climbed to $589.98 million in the January-to-June period from $484.84 million in the same period last year. The company’s revenues expanded by more than a quarter to $1.92 billion from $1.51 billion a year ago, helping offset the faster increase in expenses. ICTSI said its expenses surged 39 percent to $529.34 million in the first six months as it incurred higher operating expenses (opex) and fuel costs due to the conflict in the Middle East. The company also had to contend with unfavorable foreign exchange (forex) effects, mainly involving the Brazilian real, Mexican peso, and Australian dollar. These were partly offset by cost optimization measures and favorable forex effects from the depreciation of the Philippine peso. Global trade demand remained robust in the first half, with ICTSI handling a combined volume of 8.16 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), up 16 percent from 6.99 million TEUs a year ago. In fact, trade volume in Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) soared 43 percent as of end-June, while volumes in the Americas and Asia increased 14 percent and seven percent, respectively. The increase in trade volumes came despite disruptions in global shipping across air and sea freight networks, coupled with higher fuel costs that continued to make logistics more expensive. ICTSI Chairman and President Enrique K. Razon Jr. said this makes it crucial for the company to continue expanding its port assets in strategic locations to sustain demand for its services even as some markets experience slower growth. “Despite a more challenging operating backdrop in some markets during the period, our diversified footprint continued to provide resilience and support strong financial and operational performance,” he said in a statement. ICTSI recently added Durban Gateway Terminal in South Africa and Batu Ampar Container Terminal in Indonesia to its growing global portfolio. To sustain its growth momentum into the second half, Razon said the company remains focused on executing its expansion program and integrating its new operations. ICTSI has set aside $740 million in capital expenditures (capex) this year, of which $320.05 million, or 43 percent, had already been invested in the six months through June. The port operator is expanding its domestic facilities, including Manila International Container Terminal (MICT), Mindanao Container Terminal (MCT), and South Luzon Container Terminal (SLCT). It is also investing heavily overseas to complete expansion projects in Mexico, Brazil, and Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Under its capex program, the company is likewise funding expansion projects in Honduras, Australia, Ecuador, and Mexico. “We continue to invest to strengthen capacity and service levels across our portfolio while supporting sustainable long-term growth,” Razon said.

Fuel prices drop after monthlong surge, but LPG spikes. Motorists are set to receive a brief respite at the pump as domestic fuel prices decline in the first week of August, ending a monthlong streak of consecutive weekly increases, according to data from the Department of Energy (DOE). Effective Tuesday, Aug. 4, retail prices for diesel will drop by at least ₱0.60 per liter, while gasoline prices will decrease by ₱0.73 per liter. Kerosene will experience the largest reduction among liquid fuels, falling by ₱2.09 per liter. The downward adjustments come as international crude benchmarks retreat from recent highs following subtle shifts in global supply conditions and geopolitical sentiment. However, household budgets face an offset as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices move in the opposite direction. Cooking gas is scheduled to jump by ₱3.67 per kilogram for the month of August, driven by higher international contract prices. The adjustment adds roughly ₱40.38 to the cost of a standard 11-kilogram LPG cylinder, dampening the net financial relief for everyday consumers. Despite the persistent volatility across global energy markets, official inventory figures indicate that domestic supply levels remain robust. Latest figures from the Department of Energy showed the Philippines maintains approximately 45.22 days of total crude and petroleum product reserves. Gasoline inventories stood at 40.50 days of demand, while diesel stockpiles have risen to 47.32 days. Kerosene holds the largest buffer at approximately 132.86 days. Meanwhile, LPG supplies remain the most constrained relative to demand, standing at 35.60 days. The easing of domestic pump prices reflects changing dynamics in international markets. The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, known collectively as OPEC+, recently agreed to raise production quotas by roughly 188,000 barrels starting next month, signaling a gradual restoration of output. Market sentiment has also been tempered by geopolitical developments in the Middle East. Reports indicating that the United States may temporarily halt strikes concerning Iran to pursue renewed diplomatic talks have helped stabilize global crude benchmarks. While geopolitical risks and supply chain vulnerabilities continue to linger, the combination of expanded output quotas and diplomatic efforts offers temporary relief to import-reliant nations like the Philippines.

Workers rally at Pasig court over halted P85 wage hike. Around 100 members of labor groups and workers’ coalitions staged a protest outside the Pasig City Regional Trial Court on Monday, Aug. 3, opposing the temporary restraining order (TRO) that halted the implementation of the P85 minimum wage increase in Metro Manila. The rally took place outside Pasig RTC Branch 152 during the first hearing on the petition to stop the enforcement of Wage Order No. NCR-27. The wage order, issued by the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board–National Capital Region, mandates an P85 increase in the daily minimum wage of private sector workers in Metro Manila. Its implementation, however, remains suspended pending further court proceedings. Protesters carried placards with messages such as “Dagdag sahod namin huwag agawin (Do not take away our wage increase),” “Nakakabuhay na sahod P1,200 nationwide (A living wage of P1,200 nationwide),” and “Naging bigas na sana yung P85, na-holdap pa ni judge (The P85 could have bought rice, but the judge took it away).” Meanwhile, the Pasig City Police Station said the rally remained peaceful. Pasig City police chief Col. Hendrix Mangaldan reported that security measures were in place and maximum tolerance was observed throughout the protest. He added that the demonstrators voluntarily dispersed without incident. The Pasig City Police Station said it will continue to ensure public safety through police visibility and proactive security deployment in coordination with the Pasig City government and other stakeholders.

Alapag, Chot reunion as NLEX stakes clean slate vs TNT. For the first time, Jimmy Alapag will have a reunion with his former team TNT where he carved out his legendary PBA career. However, he would be on the other side of the court as he tries to steer his current team NLEX to its sixth straight win against TNT in the PBA Season 50 Governors’ Cup at the Ninoy Aquino Stadium on Tuesday, Aug. 4. Tip-off the clash is at 7:30 p.m. with the Road Warriors staking their unbeaten record against the resilient Tropang 5G, who, despite playing shorthanded, had strung together two consecutive victories against formidable teams San Miguel and Converge. Setting the table to the enticing duel is the clash between Titan Ultra and Macau in the first offering at 5:15 p.m. The Giant Risers are looking to get back at the Giant Pandas after dropping their first meeting 132-126. Coming off a 110-107 win over Converge behind a Rey Nambatac game-winner, and a 93-89 win over San Miguel following Kim Aurin’s overtime heroics, TNT head coach Chot Reyes admits the team is up for a tall task against the team of his former player and now NLEX coach. “Not only that they are unbeaten but they are playing at a very high level. Higher than any team in the league to be very honest with you. Great job coach Jimmy is doing there. I'm proud of what he’s doing,” Reyes said ahead of his first coaching chess match against Alapag. “This is going to be a really really big mountain for us but we will just approach it the way we should approach it — piece by piece and just focus on what’s in front of us and find a way to stop the juggernaut that is NLEX,” he added. The hope for TNT is to once again get big contributions from the shocktroopers especially with the continuous absence of Calvin Oftana, Jayson Castro, RR Pogoy and Jordan Heading. Even import Rahlir Hollis-Jefferson is still trying to regain his old self after coming in as replacement to TNT’s original import choice Darius Days. But Alapag isn’t letting his wards to be complacent even with their perfect record. “It’s tough to win in the PBA. I want us to not think about the record too much because there’s so much conference left to play but like I told the guys, this is a compliment to their work ethic and fighting spirit which is why we are here right now,” said the former NBA assistant coach.

11 hurt in Kabankalan City Charter Day fireworks blast. BACOLOD CITY – Eleven persons were injured in a fireworks explosion during the culmination of the 29th Charter Day celebration and first Kabuganaan Festival in Barangay 4, Kabankalan City, Negros Occidental on Sunday night, Aug. 2. The victims were a 17-year-old student, an Army reservist, government employee, event production staff, sound operators, office staff, teacher, and production manager. Fire Officer 3 Alfie Gravela, officer-in-charge and chief arson investigator of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP)-Kabankalan, said that fireworks allegedly malfunctioned and prematurely exploded on the ground instead of being launched into the air during a fireworks display manned by fireworks operators. Shrapnel and debris struck several spectators and event personnel. Police secured the area to prevent further casualties and emergency medical responders and other concerned agencies rendered assistance and transported the injured to the hospital. Gravela said that all victims were treated and discharged from the hospital. The BFP-Kabankalan and the Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Unit are investigating to determine the exact cause of the explosion and establish if negligence or violations of existing laws, rules, and regulations on the use of pyrotechnic devices contributed to the incident. Kabankalan celebrated Charter Day with the theme "Kabuganaan sang Kabankalan, Kadalag-an Para sa Tanan” to highlight another milestone in the city's journey to growth and progress.

Why wetlands matter more than ever. “Wetlands are weird,” said Dr. Jerome L. Montemayor, executive director of the Laguna-based ASEAN Centre for Biodiversity. “To those who are unfamiliar, it either looks like a muddy lake or a waterlogged forest. But after years in this field, you will definitely learn to appreciate these valuable natural resources and say that wetlands certainly have more than meets the eye.” Paul A. Keddy, author of “Wetland Ecology: Principles and Conservation,” defines a wetland as “an ecosystem that arises when inundation by water produces soil dominated by anaerobic processes which, in turn, forces the biota, particularly rooted plants, to adapt to flooding.” A patch of land that develops pools of water after a rainstorm would not be considered a wetland, even though the land is wet. Specifically, wetlands are characterized by a water table that stands at or near the land surface for a prolonged period each year, allowing aquatic plants to thrive. Wetlands are vital ecosystems in the country's natural environment. They are classified into three main types: freshwater, estuarine, and marine. These include natural wetlands such as rivers, lakes, swamps, marshes, peatlands, ponds, mangrove forests, seagrass meadows, and reef flats, as well as man-made wetlands such as dams and rice fields. “As an archipelago, we are shaped by water,” explained Robert E.A. Borje, Vice Chairperson and Executive Director of the Climate Change Commission, the country’s lead policy-making body on climate change. “Mangroves line our coasts, wetlands sit at river mouths and floodplains, and inland marshes and lakes regulate rainfall and runoff.” According to Borje, these ecosystems serve as an initial barrier against concentrated climate hazards. They are where storm surges lose intensity, floodwaters spread instead of wreaking havoc, and risks are reduced before they escalate into disasters. The United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) calls wetlands “the unsung heroes of the climate crisis.” Wetlands store more carbon than any other ecosystem, with peatlands, a particular type of vegetated wetland, alone storing twice as much carbon as all of the world’s forests. “Wetlands regulate water and store carbon in ways no engineered system can fully replicate,” Borje said. “They temper floods, blunt storm surges, and lock away carbon accumulated over centuries. When intact, they quietly reduce climate risk. When degraded, that risk is transferred, often directly into towns, infrastructure, and public budgets.” One often overlooked aspect of wetlands is the communities that surround them. “They do not just depend on these natural resources for their livelihood and sustenance,” Montemayor said. “In return, they also become the de facto guardians of wetlands. Bound by a shared sense of responsibility, they are keepers of tradition and knowledge that is handed over to future generations.” In the past, wetlands served as sites for human habitation, spiritual significance, and food production, reflecting sustainable interactions between people and the natural environment. Around the world, more than one billion people depend on wetlands for their livelihoods. About 40 percent of all plant and animal species – from insects to ducks and moose – live or breed in their shallow waters. Wetlands also act as extraordinary natural water filters. According to the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment, they trap sediments and absorb pollutants, significantly improving water quality. “As water flows through these ecosystems, wetland vegetation and soil microorganisms break down contaminants, such as excess nutrients and harmful chemicals,” the assessment noted. This natural filtration process not only purifies water but also prevents pollutants from reaching larger bodies of water, such as rivers and lakes. The role is especially important in agricultural areas, where runoff carries fertilizers and pesticides into streams, causing algal blooms and reducing oxygen levels in aquatic ecosystems. “Aside from their role as natural water reservoirs, wetlands serve as barriers against strong winds, heavy rain, and rising sea levels,” said Theresa Mundita Lim, former executive director of the Biodiversity Management Bureau. “Wetlands are essential habitats for a variety of fish, animals, birds, insects, shellfish, and amphibians. They also serve as abundant sources of food and breeding sites for migratory waterbirds.” But these wetlands, along with lakes, rivers, and other aquatic ecosystems around the world, are in peril. UNEP said wetlands are disappearing three times faster than forests, with more than 35 percent of wetlands worldwide degraded or lost since the 1970s. “In the Philippines, land conversion, reclamation, pollution, and poorly planned development continue to erode wetlands even as climate impacts intensify,” Borje said. “The result is not simply environmental loss. It is heightened exposure: more flooding, greater storm damage, higher recovery costs, and deeper disruptions to food systems and local economies.” “Depending on the extent of climate-related sea level rise, some 20 to 90 percent of current coastal wetlands could be gone by the end of the century,” UNEP warned. The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) stressed the need to reverse this trend. “If this trend continues, the world will lose valuable ecosystems which deliver unrivalled benefits to humanity,” the DENR said. “Wetlands do that work quietly — absorbing, slowing, and buffering risk day after day,” Borje reminded. “Keeping this natural shield in place is one of the most practical, disciplined, and forward-looking decisions the Philippines has made. This is a decision we must continue to strengthen and broaden in its implementation nationwide.”

Over 6,300 families affected as ‘Luis’ threatens Luzon – OCD. Tropical Depression Luis has affected more than 6,300 families and disrupted sea travel in several areas even as state weather forecasters warned that the cyclone could still make landfall or pass close to Northern Luzon by Monday night, Aug. 3, or early Tuesday, Aug. 4. The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said in its 6 a.m. situation report that 6,316 families were affected in Bicol (Region 5), Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9), and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). The agency also reported no deaths, injuries, or missing persons as of the latest assessment. Seven flooded areas remained under monitoring in Region 9 and BARMM while data on damaged houses and evacuation centers were still unavailable. The weather disturbance also affected sea travel as the OCD said nine trips were cancelled in Calabarzon (Region 4A) and Region 5, leaving 477 passengers, 47 rolling cargoes, and five vessels stranded. Meanwhile, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) reported that from midnight to 4 a.m. Monday, it monitored three ports affected with 491 passengers, truck drivers, cargo helpers, 45 rolling cargoes and five vessels stranded due to Luis. The stranded passengers were monitored at Real Port and Jomalig Port in Quezon, and Tabaco Port in Albay. No motorbancas were reported taking shelter. By noon, however, conditions had improved as the PCG Command Center said it monitored “no stranded passengers, vessels, rolling cargoes, and motorbancas in all ports nationwide.” It added that “all shipping and fishing operations have resumed their normal operations.” For its part, a total of P280,500 worth of assistance has been released to affected residents in Bicol by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Earlier, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) warned that Luis continued moving toward Northern Luzon. In its latest tropical cyclone bulletin, PAGASA said Luis will “move generally northwestward and may make landfall or pass close to Northern Luzon tonight or tomorrow (04 August) early morning.” As of the latest advisory, the center of Luis was estimated over the coastal waters of Palanan, Isabela while moving north northwest at 15 kilometers per hour with maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour and gusts of up to 60 kilometers per hour. PAGASA maintained Wind Signal No. 1 over affected areas and warned that the southwest monsoon and the cyclone's circulation could bring strong to gale-force gusts across most of Luzon and the Visayas through Tuesday. Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels were also advised to take precautionary measures and, if possible, avoid going out to sea in areas with moderate sea conditions.

Women legislators launch country's first Women and Children's Crisis Center. The country's first Women and Children's Crisis Center was formally launched on Monday, Aug. 3, at The Haven for Women in Alabang, Muntinlupa City through a partnership among the Philippine Congress, national government agencies, the City Government of Muntinlupa, and the private sector. Pangasinan 4th District Rep. Gina de Venecia spearheaded the project with Bulacan 4th District Rep. Linabelle Villarica, co-presidents of the Association of Women Legislators Foundation, Inc. (AWLFI), together with Bukidnon 3rd District Rep. Audrey Zubiri, the Lady Legislators of the House of Representatives, and the Senate of the Philippines. Joining the collaboration are the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) led by Secretary Rex Gatchalian, the Department of Health (DOH) under Secretary Brix Pujalte, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) led by Secretary Vince Dizon, the Congressional Spouses Foundation, Inc. headed by Mrs. Ann Dy, and the local government of Muntinlupa under Mayor Ruffy Biazon. The initiative supports President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.'s priority to strengthen mental health services, as highlighted in his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA), while expanding protection and holistic support for vulnerable sector members. Once operational, the center will provide psychiatric and psychological care, crisis intervention, trauma-informed treatment, rehabilitation, and recovery programs in a safe and dignified environment. The facility was designed by Archion Architects, led by renowned architect Dan Lichauco, whose portfolio includes major healthcare projects such as the Philippine General Hospital Felicidad Sy Multi-Specialty Building, the Asian Hospital and Medical Center Tower 2 Expansion, the National Children’s Hospital, and the Overseas Filipino Workers (OFW) Hospital in Pampanga. Rep. de Venecia underscored the importance of the project, saying, “Mental health is a fundamental human right, and every Filipina deserves access to compassionate,dignified, and world-class care during her most vulnerable moments.” De Venecia said the project reflects a collective commitment to ensure that women facing mental health challenges and crisis receive compassionate and world-class care, while Villarica described the facility as a sanctuary where survivors can heal and rebuild their lives. She added, “This Women and Children’s Crisis Center embodies our collective commitment to protect women, restore hope, strengthen families, and ensure that no woman faces mental health challenges or crisis alone.” Emphasizing the long-term impact of the initiative, Rep. Villarica stated, “Beyond providing immediate refuge, our goal is to offer a comprehensive sanctuary where survivors receive the full spectrum of care they need to heal and rebuild their lives.” “Through this multi-sectoral endeavor, we are setting a new benchmark for public care and legislative action in defense of women and children,” she added. Construction will proceed at The Haven for Women compound in Alabang, with targeted completion in 2027. Beyond serving Metro Manila, the project is envisioned as a national model for similar centers to be replicated across the regions, expanding access to specialized mental health and rehabilitation services nationwide.

SMC lists ₱30-billion preferred shares after 3.3x oversubscribed offering. Diversified conglomerate San Miguel Corp. (SMC) listed ₱30 billion worth of preferred shares on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Monday, Aug. 3, following a successful follow-on offering (FOO). PSE President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Ramon S. Monzon commended SMC for its successful preferred share issuance and for raising the largest amount from FOOs in the past seven years. “SMC has raised the most capital from follow-on offerings in the market since 2020. Including the shares to be listed today, SMC has raised a total of ₱146.65 billion from the issuance of 11 preferred share subseries spanning five FOOs,” he noted. Monzon added, “With a track record like that, SMC might as well stand for stock market champion—at least in terms of fundraising. Further cementing this title is the market’s consistent overwhelming demand for SMC’s preferred shares; this specific offering alone was oversubscribed by 3.27 times.” SMC listed its Series 2V, 2W, and 2X preferred shares on the PSE under the ticker symbols SMC2V, SMC2W, and SMC2X. SMC2V, SMC2W, and SMC2X carry dividend rates of 8.0401 percent, 8.357 percent, and 8.6483 percent, respectively. The FOO consisted of a base offer of 266.67 million shares with an oversubscription option of up to 133.33 million shares at ₱75 per share. The funds were raised as SMC manages a heavy capital expenditure (capex) cycle, led by its massive airport developments. The company earmarked up to ₱5 billion of the proceeds for an equity infusion into its infrastructure arm within 12 months of the issuance. The capital will primarily fund the New Manila International Airport (NMIA) and the surrounding aerotropolis infrastructure projects in Bulakan town, Bulacan province, just north of Metro Manila. The bulk of the capital, however, will be deployed toward debt management. If the oversubscription option is fully exercised, SMC will allocate ₱6.31 billion to pare down short-term loans with Sy-led BDO Unibank Inc. totaling ₱6.62 billion. This includes a ₱5.17-billion facility drawn on May 25, 2026, and due on June 29, 2027, alongside a ₱1.45-billion loan maturing on June 3, 2027, which was originally used to redeem Series 2-I preferred shares. From the ₱20-billion base offer, the conglomerate will utilize up to ₱6.02 billion to settle its 10-year, 5.7613-percent Series C bonds maturing in March 2027. Another ₱13.81 billion from the base portion—rising to ₱17.44 billion if the oversubscription option is exercised—is designated to retire its five-year, 5.2704-percent Series J bonds, which also mature in March 2027. Any funding shortfall will be covered by SMC’s internal cash generation. Prior to disbursement, the net proceeds will be held in short-term liquid instruments. - James A. Loyola

Archbishop hails Eala as youth role model. Alex Eala’s impact is now extending beyond the tennis court, with her rapid rise inspiring not only sports fans but also religious leaders who regard her as a role model for the country’s youth. Among them is Cebu Archbishop Alberto Uy, who urged young Filipinos to value character over trophies and fame, citing Eala as an example of humility, perseverance and gratitude despite her growing success on the international stage. “My dear young people, dream big, work hard, and never stop learning. But above all, build a beautiful character,” Uy said in a pastoral reflection. “Trophies will one day gather dust, records will eventually be broken, and fame will fade,” he added. “But humility, kindness, honesty, perseverance, and faith will continue to touch lives for generations.” Uy's message came at a time when incidents of school violence have become increasingly prevalent across the country, underscoring his call for Filipinos to prioritize character and compassion. “This is exactly what every young Filipino is called to do. Success is a blessing, but a life that inspires others to become better is an even greater blessing,” he said. “If more Filipinos choose this path, I truly believe that the future of our nation will be brighter, stronger, and filled with God’s blessings,” he added.

ERC approves urgent 67% electricity surcharge hike. Electricity consumers face higher monthly power bills starting this August after energy regulators granted urgent approval to raise a line-item surcharge that subsidizes renewable power developers. The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) issued a provisional authority allowing state-owned National Transmission Corp. (TransCo) to implement a Feed-in-Tariff Allowance (FTI-All) rate of ₱0.3359 per kilowatt-hour. The new tariff is a 67 percent increase from the current charge of ₱0.2011 per kilowatt-hour. For a residential household consuming 200 kilowatt-hours a month, the adjustment will translate to an additional charge of approximately ₱67.18 on the FIT-All line item of their monthly bill. The FIT-All is a uniform component billed by power distribution utilities to end-users and subsequently remitted to TransCo. The collected proceeds are pooled into a dedicated fund to settle guaranteed fixed payments to eligible clean energy developers whose facilities supply power to the national grid. The ERC cited an urgent liquidity crunch in approving the interim rate adjustment. The safety buffer of the fund—known as the Working Capital Allowance—has plummeted by more than 50 percent. The capital shortfall occurred after last year’s approved rate hike was delayed until November, leaving TransCo with only two months of collection to build up required reserves for 2026. “Considering the urgent need to preserve the financial viability of the FIT-All Fund and to ensure the continuous and timely payment of obligations to FIT-Eligible RE Plants, the Commission finds it reasonable and justified to authorize the provisional implementation of the proposed WCA Rate Adjustment,” the regulator stated in its order. The commission noted that the rate increase remains a temporary measure while it continues to evaluate TransCo’s petition for a final determination. Granting interim relief provides TransCo with the required lead time to collect sufficient funds and stabilize the capital buffer. The provisional rate granted by regulators is higher than TransCo’s original application seeking a charge of ₱0.2154 per kilowatt-hour, an amount the state entity previously calculated to clear back-payments owed to clean energy suppliers spanning 2016 through 2026. The regulatory intervention highlights the challenges facing Philippine energy officials as they attempt to balance the financial sustainability of green energy infrastructure with consumer affordability amid persistent cost-of-living pressures.

Cheaper power key to sustaining Philippine growth after upper-middle-income shift—World Bank. The World Bank urged the Philippines to accelerate power sector reforms to lower electricity costs and reduce its dependence on imported fuel, saying cheaper and more reliable power has become critical to sustaining economic growth, attracting investments, and reducing poverty after the country’s transition to upper-middle-income-country (UMIC) status. In its latest Philippines Economic Update (PEU) titled “Powering Progress: Electricity, Competitiveness, and Growth Pathways,” the first PEU edition released since the country attained UMIC status, the World Bank said the prolonged war in the Middle East—which disrupted global energy markets and heightened concerns over oil supply—underscored the country’s vulnerability to external shocks and reinforced the need to strengthen energy security through accelerated investments in renewable energy (RE), transmission infrastructure, energy storage, and more competitive electricity markets. “Because the Philippines is a net energy importer, when there is a global price spike in oil and gas... the costs of its imports have risen up significantly,” World Bank Philippines senior country economist Jaffar Al-Rikabi, the midyear 2026 PEU’s lead author, noted during the report’s launch on Monday, Aug. 3. The Washington-based multilateral lender cited that the Philippines imports nearly 98 percent of its crude oil requirements from the Middle East, while about 78 percent of the country’s electricity generation comes from fossil fuels. It also warned that domestic natural gas production from the Malampaya field is expected to begin declining as early as 2027, increasing the urgency of reducing reliance on imported fuels. According to the report, Philippine electricity prices remain among the highest in Southeast Asia due not only to fuel costs but also to structural issues such as concentrated power generation, transmission constraints, and limited market competition. These high power costs weaken manufacturing competitiveness, raise business operating costs, and leave the country more exposed to external price shocks. Residential electricity tariffs in the Philippines average about $0.21 per kilowatt-hour (kWh), compared with around $0.13/kWh in Thailand, $0.09/kWh in Indonesia, and $0.05/kWh in Malaysia. The World Bank said implementing an accelerated least-cost power development pathway could raise the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) by more than one percent by 2030, generate more than 161,000 additional jobs, and lift around 730,000 Filipinos out of poverty while lowering electricity prices, improving supply reliability, and reducing exposure to imported fuel. The report said the reforms include accelerating the rollout of least-cost RE, expanding transmission infrastructure, investing in battery energy storage systems (BESS), strengthening competition in the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM), and improving procurement and planning across the power sector. It also projects electricity demand to increase sharply over the coming decades, driven by the rapid expansion of data centers, artificial intelligence (AI), electric vehicles (EVs), and urbanization. Beyond the power sector, the World Bank said the Philippines’ transition to UMIC status does not eliminate longstanding structural challenges, warning that sustaining faster growth and reducing poverty will require deeper reforms. The lender forecasts Philippine gross domestic product (GDP) growth to slow to 3.7 percent this year from 4.4 percent in 2025 before recovering to 5.2 percent in 2027 as inflation eases, public investment improves, and private demand gradually strengthens. Inflation is projected to average 5.8 percent in 2026, well above last year’s 1.7 percent and the government’s two- to four-percent target. Despite the country’s graduation to UMIC status, the World Bank expects poverty reduction to proceed at a slower pace over the next two years as elevated inflation and below-trend economic growth continue to weigh on lower-income households. The lender projects the national poverty rate to decline only gradually—from 15.5 percent in 2025 to 15.3 percent in 2026 and 14.9 percent in 2027—equivalent to about 17.3 million Filipinos living below the poverty line this year before easing to around 17.1 million next year. According to the World Bank, sustaining faster poverty reduction will require stronger and more inclusive economic growth, better-quality jobs, and reforms that raise productivity—including lower electricity costs, which it identified as a key constraint to investment, competitiveness, and employment generation. Among the key risks cited by the World Bank are a prolonged disruption in Middle East oil supplies, renewed geopolitical tensions, weaker global demand, and a sharper-than-expected slowdown in the global AI investment cycle, all of which could dampen the Philippines’ growth prospects. “The national ambition of having a middle class society where nobody’s poor is achievable within a generation. It requires a commitment to reforms and to their implementation,” Gonzalo Varela, World Bank lead economist covering the Philippines, Malaysia, and Brunei, said during the report’s launch. - Danielle T. Bayani

Castro: Pax Silica won't affect farmers. The proposed Pax Silica artificial intelligence (AI) industrial hub in Tarlac will not affect farmers, a Palace official said. Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro pointed out that no farmers will be affected by the development of the controversial AI hub as there should no longer be farmers in the area approved as "buildable zones." Castro explained that since the Southeast Asian (SEA) Games in 2019, "buildable areas have already been established and allocated." "So, sa lugar na ito ay dapat wala ng farmers dahil ito po nga ay na-approve na bilang buildable zones (Therefore, there should no longer be farmers in these areas because they have already been approved as buildable zones)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Monday, Aug. 3. "At mayroon naman pong natitira na 6,000 hectares na reserve para sa open green spaces, forest reserves and designated zones for upland farming (There are still 6,000 hectares reserved for open green spaces, forest reserves, and designated zones for upland farming)," Castro added. The Palace official further pointed out that the project will occupy only "a relatively small portion of the area." "So, maliit lang po ang maookupa nito – 3,500 hectares ang kabuuan ng buildable zones at doon po maaaring ilagay itong proyekto regarding Pax Silica (The project will occupy only a relatively small portion of the area. The total buildable zones cover 3,500 hectares, and this is where the proposed Pax Silica project may be located)," Castro said. "So, hindi po makakaapekto ito sa ating mga farmers (So, this project will not affect our farmers)," she stressed. The Palace spokesperson made the remarks when sought for reaction to Senator Imee Marcos' call for an investigation into complaints that farmers are allegedly being ordered to stop planting and are facing intimidation as the government continues its pursuit of the Pax Silica initiative. Castro said the President's sister is free to pursue any investigation on the project, but told her that "it would be better if she were aware of the issue being discussed." "Hindi naman napipigil si Senator Imee sa kaniyang mga gusto at siguro mas maganda po na malaman niya kasi ang pinag-uusapan dito ay mga farmers (Senator Imee is certainly not being prevented from pursuing the matters she wants to raise. Perhaps it would be better if she were aware that the issue being discussed here concerns the farmers)," she said. Castro also reiterated that the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), the state-run firm overseeing the development of the Pax Silica initiative, "is open to consultations." "Sa ngayon po binanggit ko po noong nakaraan ang BCDA po ay open po at sa ngayon po ay patuloy po ang kanilang pagkokonsulta sa mga concerned agencies, concerned local government units, sa lahat ng stakeholders (As I mentioned previously, the BCDA is open to consultations. At present, it continues to engage with the concerned government agencies, local government units, and all other stakeholders)," Castro said. "Kaya ito po ay nabanggit natin para sa lahat ng may mga concerns ay maaari pong makipag-ugnayan sa ating pamahalaan para matugunan kung ano ang mga issues na dapat pang iresolba (We have emphasized this so that anyone with concerns may coordinate with the government, allowing any remaining issues to be addressed and resolved)," Castro said. Pax Silica Industrial Hub is planned for development on a stretch of land roughly 1,620 hectares inside New Clark City, Tarlac. The Philippines joined the US-led international coalition launched in December 2025 to secure supply chains for semiconductors, critical minerals, and artificial intelligence technologies. The project has been steadily opposed by a coalition of farmer groups, environmental scientists and advocates, who raise various concerns such as mass displacement, water scarcity, mining expansion and pollution, food security, economic dependency, and sovereignty and legal jurisdiction.

'Wala pa rin': Ridon still looking for VP Duterte 5 five weeks into impeachment trial. House prosecutor Bicol Saro Party-list Rep. Terry Ridon chided Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Aug. 3 for being absent--yet again--in her own Senate impeachment trial. "Sa ikalimang linggo o ikalabing-isang araw ng paglilitis, wala pa ring Vice President Sara Duterte sa loob ng Senate impeachment court," Ridon said in a short statement . (On the fifth week, or the 11th day of trial, Vice President Sara Duterte is still absent from the Senate impeachment court.) "Muli, nasaan man po kayo sa mundo Madam Vice President, harapin po natin ang paglilitis, harapin natin ang katotohanan," added the lawyer-legislator. (Once again, wherever you may be in the world Madam Vice President, let us face the trial, let us face the truth.) Ridon was seemingly alluding to the respondent's recent two-week trip abroad. The Vice President's July 16 to 31 trip covered Qatar, the United Kingdom (UK), and the Netherlands. Duterte left the country just as the prosecutors shifted to presenting evidence on article I , which delved into allegations of confidential funds misuse amounting to P612.5 million. The prosecution panel had just finished its presentation on article IV, which covered Duterte’s Nov. 23, 2024 death threats against President Marcos and other members of the First Family. Presiding officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero earlier ruled that the respondent need not personally attend the court proceedings, as she was amply represented by her counsels.

Alas Women absorb four-set loss to Indonesia, miss SEA V.Cup podium. Alas Pilipinas came out empty-handed after bowing to Indonesia, 25-20, 19-25, 22-25, 16-25, at the conclusion of the 2026 Women’s SEA V. Cup’s first leg at the Dong Anh Gymnasium in Hanoi, Vietnam Sunday, Aug. 2. Similar to their last two games, the Nationals, powered by Niña Ytang, Alyssa Solomon, and Bella Belen, stepped on the gas pedal early on to take the opening set. However, the Indonesians easily solved the riddle and stormed in the next three frames to frustrate the Filipina spikers. Despite missing out on a podium finish, Solomon brought the Nationals on the spotlight after claiming the Best Opposite Spiker plum. Indonesia, on the other hand, clinched the bronze honors with Maradanti Namira Tegariani earning the Best Middle Blocker nod. Ytang delivered a breakout game for the Taka Minowa-mentored crew with 14 points on 11 attacks, two blocks, and one ace, while Solomon and Belen chipped in 13 and 12 points, respectively. Eya Laure, Dell Palomata, and Fifi Sharma combined for 18 points in a losing cause for the Philippines. Indonesia, for its act, leaned on Arsela Nuari Purnama who scored 18 points, while Chelsa Berliana Nurtomo and Mediol Stiovanny Yoku uncorked 16 points apiece. Meanwhile, the formidable Thailand made quick work of Vietnam, 25-18, 25-17, 25-14, to keep its record pristine and capture the first leg of the annual tournament. With all teams set for a three-day break, the Philippines will look to finally break into the win column when it faces host Thailand on Friday, Aug. 7, at the Chiang Mai Sports Complex.

Batangas cops seize 193 illegal firearms. BATANGAS CITY – Batangas police seized 193 loose firearms during operations in the province from May to July. Police Col. Oliver Ebora, Batangas police chief, presented these to Police Brig. Gen. Dominic Baccay, Police Regional Office 4-A director, during his visit Monday, Aug. 3. Baccay cited operating units for their achievements that prevented the proliferation of firearms on the streets that may be used to commit crimes. He assured that the campaign won’t stop until the province is rid of all loose firearms. These will be turned over to crime laboratory for ballistic examination. Baccay urged owners of unlicensed firearms to voluntarily surrender their weapons. The Police Regional Office 4-A said Monday that 1,208 drug personalities and illegal drugs valued at P29.6 million were seized during 942 operations in the Calabarzon region from July 1 to July 31. Baccay said operating units recovered 4,333.59 grams of shabu, 245.58 grams of marijuana, and 43.46 grams of kush. He vowed to sustain aggressive anti-illegal drug operations and ensure that those who continue to violate the law are brought to justice. Suspects are in the custody of arresting units and facing appropriate charges for violating Republic Act No. 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.

PH women’s lacrosse team finishes 10th; USA completes five-peat. The Philippine women’s lacrosse team settled for 10th place after absorbing a 9-10 overtime loss to Argentina in the 2026 World Lacrosse Women's Championship at the Oi Hockey Stadium in Tokyo, Japan over the weekend. Gaining momentum from their 12-4 victory over Wales, the Nationals tried to assert their dominance anew but saw themselves in a tight encounter against the Argentines. The Philippines, sparked by Steph Lazo’s offensive rally, dug deep in the extended period but it was Argentina that delivered the coup de grace after Olivia Duarte won the opening draw which eventually led to Emilia DiLiberto’s fourth goal to close out their thrilling showdown. Lazo starred for the Filipina bets with three goals, while Caroline Roxas, Ria Lagdameo, Abby Manalang, Kalena Johnson, and Annika Bennett contributed one goal each. Abigail Beattie also shone with five saves. On the other hand, Diliberto stood out with four goals, while Gretta White and Duarte found the net twice for the South American country. Although Argentina secured ninth place, the Philippines still turned heads in its first-ever appearance at the World Championship after finishing 10th overall. Head coach Shannon Nee believes it showcased the Filipinas' capability to compete on the global stage. “With close matches against the host country Japan and the overtime loss to Argentina, we have just tapped into what this team can accomplish,” said Nee. “Our young ones played fearlessly and our veterans showed leadership in difficult moments.” The Philippines posted a 2-3 win-loss record in the group stage and classification round. It became the second-best Asian team in the quadrennial meet just behind 7th Japan (3-3) and ahead of 15th Chinese Taipei (1-4). Up next for the locals is the APLU Sixes Championship in Queensland, Australia this October. Meanwhile, the United States flexed its might and dismantled Canada, 16-4, in their all-North Americans finals to complete a perfect campaign en route to its fifth straight championship.

PH booters face unbeaten Thais in crucial match. The Philippine men's national football team makes its home stand when it faces unbeaten Thailand in the 2026 ASEAN Championship (Hyundai Cup) at the New Clark City Stadium in Capas, Tarlac Tuesday, Aug. 4. Following their 4-1 victory over Laos, the Nationals (1-1) look forward to maintaining their form against the Thais (2-0) in their Group B clash set at 9 p.m., with a victory for the Filipinos boosting their chances of clinching a semis berth in the biennial meet. The Philippines, which currently sits at fourth spot behind seven-time champion Thailand and Malaysia (2-1), eyes the crucial win with only the top two squads advancing to the semis It is tied with Myanmar in terms of record as both squads sport a similar 1-1 slate worth three points. A loss could be fatal for the Carles Cuadrat-mentored crew which previously reached the semis of the regional joust. For Cuadrat, their recent triumph against Laos gave the Filipino booters a sort of a morale boost after failing to convert several opportunities in their opening game loss to Myanmar. “Most importantly, I am happy that we changed our fortunes,” said Cuadrat. “Until this match, we had been very unfortunate during several important moments. “The victory is a good reward for the squad, and we must now focus on our next match,” he added. Cole Mrowka, last game’s Player of the Match, spearheads the Nationals anew with Jarvey Gayoso, John Lucero, and Daisuke Sato providing support.

Imee Marcos files resolution seeking Senate probe into Pax Silica project. Senator Imee Marcos on Monday, August 3 has formally filed a resolution urging the Senate to look into the proposed Pax Silica project’s impact on the water and electricity resource demands and long-term environmental impacts on the country’s natural resources. Marcos made the call in light of reports the Pax Silica Initiative in New Clark City, Capas, Tarlac, is already underway despite lack of community consultation and feasibility studies. President Marcos’ sister said the goal of Senate Resolution No. 547 is to strengthen the country’s current laws and regulatory frameworks to safeguard water, energy and food security, and also promote environmental sustainability. The senator pointed out that the biggest concern raised by environmental and scientific organizations is not the technology itself, but the enormous amount of water and electricity needed to keep Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems and large-scale data centers running. "Because unlike conventional office buildings, AI data centers and servers inevitably generate intense heat and must be continuously cooled to prevent equipment failure which require vast quantities of clean water, while the servers themselves require a stable and uninterrupted electricity supply 24 hours a day,” Marcos stated in the explanatory note of SRN 547. Last April 2026, the Philippines joined the Pax Silica, a United States-led initiative on AI and supply chain security, which seeks to balance global tech manufacturing capacities, particularly in semiconductor fabrication, computing component processing and critical earth material procurement. Other countries that joined the Pax Silica Initiative also include Japan, South Korea, Singapore, United Kingdom, Israel, United Arab Emirates, Australia, Finland, Sweden, Qatar and India. But Marcos said the initial impact assessments indicate that semiconductor manufacturing, AI data center cooling, and critical mineral processing hub will demand an estimated 130 million liters of water per day, a volume equivalent to the daily consumption of roughly 600,000 households, as well as three (3) gigawatts of electricity, representing a least 16 percent of Luzon’s current grid capacity. While the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) has stated that the proposed hub will utilize surface water and water-impounding technologies capable of supplying up to 90 million liters of water per day without affecting community water sources, she said concerns remain as to whether such measures are sufficient enough to meet the project’s water demands and adequately protect surrounding communities and the environment. “While the Pax Silica initiative promises significant long-term economic growth, foreign direct investment (FDI), and job creation, serious concerns persist regarding its heavy footprint on local land use, rural agricultural livelihoods, ecological stability and environmental sustainability,” she said. Moreover, she said the country’s agriculture and food security may also be adversely affected, as increased demand for water and other resources could reduce access to irrigation for farmers, increase utility costs for households, worsen land displacement, suppress wages, cause environmental degradation and place additional pressures on the lands and livelihoods of local and indigenous communities. “There is an urgent need to determine whether existing laws, including the Water Code of the Philippines (Presidential Decree No. 1067) and the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004 (Republic Act No. 9275), among other relevant statutes, remain adequate to regulate emerging industries, or whether additional legislative safeguards are necessary to ensure that agricultural productivity and environmental sustainability are prioritized over industrial allocation,” the lawmaker stressed.

Visa, GCash to launch seamless link-and-pay feature for faster, more convenient payment experience. Visa and GCash will launch a new and more secure payment experience allowing consumers to use Visa cards as a funding source for QR transactions in the GCash app. The new capability gives consumers greater security and flexibility in how they pay, enabling them to link eligible Visa cards to GCash and use them for everyday purchases anywhere GCash is accepted. Previously, when consumers lacked the wallet balance to fund transactions, they would need to top-up from linked bank accounts in their GCash app or through fund transfers from other banks. The solution will make wallet funding more seamless, enabling consumers to make QR payments at checkout through their linked Visa cards. Whether enjoying meals at restaurants, buying from weekend markets, or shopping for souvenirs across the country’s many tourist destinations, consumers can now choose the funding method that best suits their needs – all within a familiar digital wallet experience. Consumers will also be able to transact with confidence and ease as each transaction using a Visa card is protected by Visa Payment Passkey, a next-generation biometric authentication solution that allows consumers to verify online purchases using their device’s fingerprint, face recognition, or PIN instead of passwords or SMS one-time passcodes (OTP). Built on Fast Identity Online (FIDO®) standards, Visa Payment Passkey helps deliver a faster, more seamless checkout experience while enhancing protection against phishing and other forms of online fraud. Biometric authentication can reduce up to 50% of fraud rates[1] compared to SMS-based OTPs. “Consumers increasingly expect flexibility in how they pay, and are looking for payment experiences that are simple, secure, and seamless. This exciting collaboration expands that flexibility for consumers, allowing consumers to use their Visa credentials across everyday digital payment journeys including QR payments. This takes us forward in making digital payments more accessible and convenient for everyone,” said Jeffrey Navarro, Country Manager for Visa Philippines. “This new feature further enhances the GCash experience for millions of Filipinos, giving them greater freedom in how they pay and manage their funds while maintaining the experience they’ve come to expect from GCash. This partnership also reinforces our shared trust with Visa to expand financial inclusion and bring more Filipinos into the digital economy,” added Ren-Ren Reyes, President & CEO of G-Xchange, Inc. (the mobile wallet operator of GCash) According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), digital transactions now account for 57.4% of total monthly retail volume in the Philippines[2]. Enabling card-funded QR payments accelerates this digital shift and reinforces Visa's broader strategy of enabling consumers to pay wherever and however they choose. By supporting innovative payment experiences across cards, wallets, and QR payments, Visa and GCash continue to help drive the growth of digital commerce and advance financial inclusion across the Philippines.

PFF emphasizes team resilience despite Hyundai Cup challenges. The Philippine Men’s National Football Team reignited its 2026 ASEAN Championship – Hyundai Cup campaign with a rousing 4-1 comeback victory over Laos in Vientiane. But for Philippine Football Federation (PFF) President John Anthony Gutierrez, the triumph was defined not only by the scoreline but by the circumstances under which it was achieved. Despite those constraints, the PH football chief praised the resilience and commitment of the squad that took the field. “We are incredibly proud of every player who answered the call to represent our country. We believe in this team, and we support them one hundred percent—win or lose,” said Gutierrez. ``They have our full confidence because we know the commitment, sacrifice, and pride they bring every time they play for country,’’ he added. The Philippines overturned a 1-0 halftime deficit with four unanswered goals in the second half, showcasing the depth and determination of the players who stepped up in the absence of others tied to club duties. Goals from John Lucero, Jarvey Gayoso, Daisuke Sato, and a Laos own goal sealed the country’s first win of the tournament. “Every football nation experiences victories and defeats. What matters is how a team responds, how it continues to improve, and how it grows over time. This victory is an important response, but it is also another step in our journey of building a stronger Philippine national team for the future,” said Gutierrez. The PFF President also expressed his appreciation to Filipino fans for expressing their support for the team. ``We are deeply grateful to every Filipino who continues to support our national team. To those who celebrated with us, thank you. To those who criticize us, we know those emotions come from your passion and your desire to see Philippine football succeed,’’ said Gutierrez. ``But football is also about respect. The only way to move Philippine football forward is if we all work together with respect, united by the beautiful game we all love,’’ added Gutierrez. Gutierrez also emphasized the unique difficulties of the Hyundai Cup, which is staged outside the FIFA International Match Calendar. “The Hyundai Cup is not played during a FIFA international window. Despite the Philippine Football Federation’s best efforts to appeal to international clubs to release our players, not everyone was available for national team duty because of their club commitments,’’ Gutierrez explained. ``That is the reality not only for the Philippines but for many teams in this competition,” he added. The result lifts the Philippines to three points in Group B, equaling its biggest-ever winning margin over Laos in the ASEAN Championship. The team now heads home for a crucial clash against Thailand on August 4 at New Clark City Stadium in Capas, Tarlac.

DOST vows responsible AI use. ILOILO CITY – As the controversy surrounding the Pax Silica initiative swirls, the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) vowed to promote responsible use of technology, especially artificial intelligence (AI). “On the side of the DOST, our role is to make sure that technology is used for responsible development,” said DOST Secretary Renato U. Solidum Jr. on the sidelines of the 2026 AI Fest in Iloilo City on Monday, Aug. 3. Solidum clarified the DOST has no direct role in Pax Silica as terms are still being negotiated by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) with the United States (US), which is leading the global initiative on a global AI supply chain. Since the country joined last April, there have been many questions about the long-term impact on the environment and the people with the proposed Pax Silica site in New Clark City, Tarlac. “I am not the person who can give assurance (about Pax Silica). It’s very difficult to discuss things without the details,” Solidum said during a press conference in Iloilo City on Monday. Solidum underscored that Pax Silica will still undergo regulatory review from the country’s government agencies. Solidum said that human resources must be upgraded to keep up with what is needed in AI in each sector.

Focus crimes down by 36.12% in July 2026-- PNP. Focus crimes across the country dropped by 36.12 percent last month compared to the same period last year, the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclosed on Monday, August 3. Focus crimes are classified into two: crimes against person which are murder, homicide, physical injury and rape; and, crimes against property which robbery, theft, carnapping and motorcycle theft. From 3,458 focus crime incidents in July last year, PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr. said it went down to 2,209 incidents last month, or a decrease of 1,249 incidents or 36.12 percent. “These results reflect the continuing efforts of the PNP, together with our communities and partner agencies, to prevent crime, strengthen police visibility, and keep our neighborhoods safe,” said Nartatez. The decline, according to Nartatez, was observed in eight focus crimes with rape posting the highest decrease at 56.93 percent, followed by motor vehicle theft by 46.15 percent, and motorcycle theft by 42.59 percent. In Western Visayas, focus crimes went down by 38.09 percent for the same month compared to the same period last year. Brig. Gen. Randulf T. Tuaño, director of the Police Regional Office 6, said focus crime incidents declined from 168 cases recorded in July 1–31, 2025 to 104 cases in the same month this year. He said rape posted the highest decrease, dropping by 78.26 percent, or from 46 cases to 10 cases; followed by carnapping of motorcycles, which declined by 76.92 percent, or from 13 cases to three cases. Murder cases decreased by 28.57 percent, or from 14 to 10 cases, while robbery declined by 15.38 percent, from 13 to 11 cases. Cases of theft dropped by 13.63 percent, or from 44 to 38 cases. Homicide remained at eight cases during both periods. "These numbers reflect the collective effort of our police officers and our communities to make Western Visayas safer. We will continue building on these gains by strengthening police visibility, improving response capabilities, and working closely with our stakeholders to prevent crime before it happens," Tuaño said. He likewise encouraged the public to remain vigilant and continue supporting law enforcement by reporting suspicious activities and incidents through the nearest police station or other official police communication channels.

When should babies start eating solid food? 6 things parents should know. A baby’s first spoonful is an exciting milestone, but it also brings questions. Is the baby ready? What should be offered, and how much? What if the baby spits everything out? Complementary feeding begins when food is introduced in addition to breast milk or formula, generally at around six months. Dr. Jayeanne M. Bihag-Lomibao, a diplomate of the Philippine Pediatric Society, says age is not the only consideration. The baby must also be developmentally ready. 1. Look for signs of readiness. Before giving a baby solid food, parents should check whether the child has good head and neck control, can sit with minimal support, shows interest in food, and opens their mouth when food is offered. Once these signs appear, she recommends bringing the baby to a pediatrician before offering solid food. “This allows us to confirm that the baby is truly ready for complementary feeding and gives us the opportunity to provide anticipatory guidance on proper feeding techniques, food choices, allergy prevention, choking safety, and other important reminders before the baby’s feeding journey begins.” 2. Begin with familiar, nutritious foods. A baby’s first meals do not have to come from a jar or cost a lot. “Families don’t need expensive commercial baby food. The best first foods are those that are soft, nutritious, and rich in iron,” Dr. Jayeanne tells Manila Bulletin Lifestyle. Many good choices are already found in Filipino kitchens, such as mashed rice or lugaw, camote, kalabasa, sayote, carrots, malunggay, pechay, banana, papaya, avocado, and ripe mango. It is also important to include iron-rich foods like egg, fish, chicken, beef, liver, and monggo. The goal is to serve different nutritious foods while continuing breast milk or formula. 3. Serve small portions and change textures gradually. At six to eight months, begin with about two to three tablespoons per meal, offered two to three times daily while milk feeds continue. The amount can gradually increase depending on the baby’s appetite. Food consistency should also change with age. Begin with mashed or puréed food before moving to minced and chopped food. By one year old, babies can begin eating family meals prepared in a way that is safe for them. Delaying textured food can make it harder for babies to practice chewing and accept different kinds of food. 4. Let babies participate. Baby-led weaning can be combined with spoon-feeding. Dr. Jayeanne suggests letting babies touch, smell, and examine suitable pieces of food while a caregiver helps feed them. This allows them to practice feeding skills while receiving enough nutrition. Keep mealtimes free from pressure and distractions. Force-feeding and using gadgets to keep a baby eating can interfere with responsive feeding, which helps caregivers recognize when the child is hungry or already full. 5. Introduce new foods safely. Common allergenic foods such as egg, peanut, fish, dairy, wheat, and soy may be offered at around six months once complementary feeding has begun. Dr. Jayeanne says delaying their introduction is no longer routinely recommended. Families with a history of atopy or a baby at higher risk of allergies should consult their pediatrician first. She also recommends introducing one new ingredient every two to three days, making it easier to identify the possible cause of a reaction. Honey should not be given to babies younger than one year because it may contain spores that cause infant botulism, a rare illness that can lead to muscle weakness and difficulty breathing. Sugary drinks, salty food, and highly processed products should also be avoided. 6. Give rejected food another chance. A baby who closes their mouth or spits out a new food is not necessarily a picky eater. Eating is still a new skill, and some foods may take time to accept. “Patience goes a long way. A food they reject today may become one of their favorite foods a few weeks later,” she adds. Continue offering small amounts without forcing the baby to finish. Keep mealtimes relaxed and try the rejected food again on another day. Ongoing feeding difficulties, poor weight gain, frequent choking or coughing while eating, recurrent vomiting, or possible signs of an allergy should be brought to a pediatrician’s attention. These first meals may come with spills and rejected bites. Dr. Jayeanne reminds families not to be discouraged, “Patience goes a long way. A food they reject today may become one of their favorite foods a few weeks later.”

Baguio launches ‘Ligtas Tigdas’ vaxx drive. BAGUIO CITY – Baguio Mayor Benjamin Magalong on Monday urged parents and guardians to have children ages six to 59 months vaccinated against measles and rubella as the Department of Health-Cordillera (DOH-CAR) launched the third phase of its "Ligtas Tigdas" supplemental immunization campaign. "Vaccination is the best gift we can give our loved ones. Let us protect our children from the serious complications of measles and rubella by bringing them for vaccination," Magalong said in a message read by Executive Assistant Leandro Tabilog during the campaign launch. The supplemental immunization drive runs from Aug. 3 to 28 and aims to vaccinate more than 150,000 children across Abra, Apayao, Benguet, Ifugao, Kalinga, Mountain Province and Baguio City. Nationwide, nearly 11 million children are targeted before the program ends later this year. DOH-CAR Regional Director Dr. Amelita Pangilinan said measles and rubella cases in the Cordillera declined by 40 percent as of July compared with the same period last year, attributing the drop to sustained vaccination efforts despite the pandemic. "This is not by accident," Pangilinan said, citing the work of barangay health workers who conducted door-to-door visits to reach children who missed routine vaccinations and the continued support of local government units. She said health workers will continue administering free vaccines at health centers and through community outreach activities during the three-week campaign. Pangilinan reminded parents that mild coughs or colds should not delay vaccination. "What should worry us most is measles itself," she said, noting that the disease spreads easily through the air and can lead to pneumonia, meningitis, blindness, or death. She emphasized that vaccines remain safe, effective, and free, noting that the country's National Immunization Program has protected millions of Filipino children over the past five decades. City Health Officer Dr. Celia Flor Brillantes said Baguio achieved an 84 percent measles-rubella vaccination rate two years ago, contributing to only four recorded cases in 2025 and four cases as of July this year. She urged residents to help spread information about the campaign and encourage parents to bring eligible children for vaccination. Vaccines are available at Baguio's 16 district rural health centers and at fixed vaccination sites operated by the Philippine Red Cross-Baguio Chapter. Meanwhile, a pediatrician from the Philippine Pediatric Society in Northern Luzon expressed support for the campaign, stressing that supplemental immunization provides added protection by closing immunity gaps and reducing the risk of outbreaks. Dr. Maria Lourdes Trajano, a pediatric neurologist and vice president of the Philippine Pediatric Society-Northern Luzon, said she has treated children with vaccine-preventable diseases and urged parents not to miss the opportunity for added protection.

Marcos' action on gambling allegations vs DOH chief depends on evidence, probe —Palace.
